art-ib-myp-myp-acting-basics.name: 表演基础
art-ib-myp-myp-acting-basics.subject: art
curriculum_points: Students in MYP years 1-2 will be able to apply fundamental acting techniques (e.g., vocal projection, physical characterization, focus) in prepared and improvised scenarios.
Students will be able to use voice, movement, and gesture intentionally to create believable characters and communicate clear intentions on stage.

art-ib-myp-myp-drawing-skills.name: 素描与观察
art-ib-myp-myp-drawing-skills.subject: art
art-ib-myp-myp-drawing-skills.domain: 视觉艺术 / Visual Arts / Visual Arts
curriculum_points: Students in MYP years 1-3 will be able to employ a range of drawing techniques (e.g., contour, gesture, tonal rendering) to accurately represent form, space, and proportion.
Students in MYP years 4-5 will be able to select and refine drawing skills purposefully to develop a personal visual language and support artistic intention in their body of work.

art-ib-myp-myp-music-reading.name: 识谱
art-ib-myp-myp-music-reading.subject: art
curriculum_points: Students in MYP years 1-3 will be able to interpret and apply standard musical notation (pitch, rhythm, dynamics, articulation) in performance and composition tasks.
Students in MYP years 4-5 will be able to fluently read and notate musical ideas using appropriate conventions, facilitating collaboration and analysis.

art-ib-myp-myp-artist-study.name: 艺术家研究
art-ib-myp-myp-artist-study.subject: art
art-ib-myp-myp-artist-study.domain: 回应与反思 / Responding & Reflection / Responding
curriculum_points: Students will be able to conduct in-depth research into the life, influences, techniques, and body of work of a selected artist, musician, or theatre practitioner.
Students will be able to critically analyze the work of studied practitioners to evaluate their impact and relevance, and draw connections to their own artistic practice.

art-ib-myp-myp-instrument.name: 乐器演奏
art-ib-myp-myp-instrument.subject: art
curriculum_points: Students will be able to develop technical proficiency on a chosen instrument or voice, demonstrating control over tone, intonation, and expressive techniques.
Students will be able to perform repertoire from diverse genres and cultures with stylistic awareness, both as a soloist and as part of an ensemble.

art-ib-myp-myp-painting-media.name: 绘画媒材
art-ib-myp-myp-painting-media.subject: art
art-ib-myp-myp-painting-media.domain: 视觉艺术 / Visual Arts / Visual Arts
curriculum_points: Students will be able to demonstrate technical competence in applying various painting media (e.g., watercolor, acrylic, gouache) to explore color theory, texture, and compositional effects.
Students will be able to make informed choices about painting materials and techniques to convey specific moods, concepts, or cultural contexts in their artwork.

art-ib-myp-myp-music-genres.name: 音乐体裁
art-ib-myp-myp-music-genres.subject: art
curriculum_points: Students will be able to identify and describe the distinguishing characteristics, cultural origins, and historical development of a range of musical genres.
Students will be able to compare and contrast musical genres, evaluating how social, historical, and technological factors influence musical style and practice.

art-ib-myp-myp-process-journal.name: 过程日志
art-ib-myp-myp-process-journal.subject: art
art-ib-myp-myp-process-journal.domain: 回应与反思 / Responding & Reflection / Responding
curriculum_points: Students will be able to document their artistic process, research, experimentation, and reflections consistently in a journal, demonstrating the development of ideas over time.
Students will use the process journal to plan, record, and evaluate their work against the MYP Arts criteria, showing evidence of critical thinking and artistic growth.

art-ib-myp-myp-scene-work.name: 剧目排练
art-ib-myp-myp-scene-work.subject: art
curriculum_points: Students in MYP years 3-5 will be able to analyze a scripted scene to make directorial and performance choices regarding character motivation, relationship, and staging.
Students will be able to collaborate effectively within an ensemble to rehearse, refine, and perform scenes, demonstrating responsiveness and stagecraft.

art-ib-myp-myp-sculpture-3d.name: 雕塑与立体
art-ib-myp-myp-sculpture-3d.subject: art
art-ib-myp-myp-sculpture-3d.domain: 视觉艺术 / Visual Arts / Visual Arts
curriculum_points: Students in MYP years 2-4 will be able to manipulate a variety of materials (e.g., clay, wire, found objects) using additive, subtractive, and construction techniques to create three-dimensional forms.
Students will be able to apply an understanding of spatial relationships, scale, and structural integrity to design and realize sculptural artworks.

art-ib-myp-myp-critique.name: 艺术评论
art-ib-myp-myp-critique.subject: art
art-ib-myp-myp-critique.domain: 回应与反思 / Responding & Reflection / Responding
curriculum_points: Students will be able to use appropriate arts terminology to describe, analyze, interpret, and evaluate artworks and performances (their own and others').
Students will be able to engage constructively in critique sessions, providing and applying feedback to refine artistic work in relation to stated intentions and criteria.

art-ib-myp-myp-printmaking.name: 版画
art-ib-myp-myp-printmaking.subject: art
art-ib-myp-myp-printmaking.domain: 视觉艺术 / Visual Arts / Visual Arts
curriculum_points: Students will be able to execute basic printmaking processes (e.g., relief, monotype) to produce multiple images, demonstrating an understanding of registration, inking, and editioning.
Students will be able to utilize the unique qualities of printmaking (e.g., repetition, variation) to explore pattern, sequence, or social commentary in their visual communication.

art-ib-myp-myp-art-history.name: 艺术史
art-ib-myp-myp-art-history.subject: art
art-ib-myp-myp-art-history.domain: 视觉艺术 / Visual Arts / Visual Arts
curriculum_points: Students will be able to identify and analyze key artworks, movements, and cultural contexts from different historical periods and global traditions.
Students will be able to investigate the connections between art historical knowledge and their own artistic development, using research to inform and contextualize their work.

art-ib-myp-myp-composition.name: 创作与编曲
art-ib-myp-myp-composition.subject: art
curriculum_points: Students will be able to create original musical pieces by structuring and developing musical ideas (melody, rhythm, harmony, texture) using appropriate tools and technology.
Students will be able to apply knowledge of musical elements and structures to compose for specific purposes, audiences, or contexts, and reflect on their creative process.

art-ib-myp-myp-digital-media.name: 数字媒体
art-ib-myp-myp-digital-media.subject: art
art-ib-myp-myp-digital-media.domain: 视觉艺术 / Visual Arts / Visual Arts
curriculum_points: Students in MYP years 3-5 will be able to use digital tools and software for creating, manipulating, and presenting still and moving images, demonstrating digital literacy.
Students will be able to critically evaluate the role of digital media in contemporary art practice and society, applying this understanding to their own creative projects.

art-ib-myp-myp-theatre-history.name: 戏剧史
art-ib-myp-myp-theatre-history.subject: art
curriculum_points: Students will be able to trace the development of theatrical forms, conventions, and practitioners from classical traditions to contemporary practice.
Students will be able to investigate how theatre reflects and influences the society and culture in which it is created, and apply this understanding to their own dramatic work.

bio-m-asexual-reproduction.name: 植物的无性生殖
bio-m-asexual-reproduction.subject: biology
curriculum_points: 无性生殖是植物繁殖的一种方式，如扦插、嫁接等，能够保持母本的优良性状。
通过观察或实验，描述植物的无性生殖过程，并举例说明其在农业生产中的应用。
组织学生开展植物扦插、嫁接等实践活动，体验无性生殖的技术方法。
chapters: 八年级下册 第6单元 生命的延续和发展

bio-m-bio-characteristics.name: 生物的基本特征
bio-m-bio-characteristics.subject: biology
curriculum_points: 细胞是生物体结构和功能的基本单位。细胞的分裂、分化和生长是细胞重要的生命活动。
识别动植物细胞的结构并说出其异同点，说明细胞是生物体结构和功能的基本单位。

bio-m-biosphere.name: 生物圈
bio-m-biosphere.subject: biology
curriculum_points: 生态系统中的生物与非生物环境相互作用，实现了物质循环和能量流动。
从结构与功能的角度，阐明生态系统中的生产者、消费者、分解者以及非生物环境是一个有机整体。
分析人类活动对生态环境造成破坏的实例，形成保护生物圈的社会责任意识。
结合具体实例，引导学生分析生态系统中各成分的作用及其相互关系，并用恰当的形式呈现，发展学生的建模思维。

bio-m-cell-division-junior.name: 细胞分化
bio-m-cell-division-junior.subject: biology
curriculum_points: 细胞能通过分裂和分化形成不同的组织
描述细胞分裂和分化的基本过程；识别人体和植物体的主要组织；说明细胞通过分裂和分化形成各种组织
引导学生通过观察某种器官不同组织的特点，基于事实进行科学推理，深入理解细胞分化的概念

bio-m-cell-division-m.name: 细胞分裂
bio-m-cell-division-m.subject: biology
curriculum_points: 细胞能通过分裂和分化形成不同的组织
描述细胞分裂和分化的基本过程；识别人体和植物体的主要组织；说明细胞通过分裂和分化形成各种组织，组织构成不同的器官
引导学生通过观察某种器官不同组织的特点，基于事实进行科学推理，深入理解细胞分化的概念
chapters: 必修一 第6章

bio-m-cell-life-activities.name: 细胞的生命活动
bio-m-cell-life-activities.subject: biology
curriculum_points: 细胞不同结构的功能各不相同，共同完成细胞的各项生命活动。
运用示意图或模型等方式，展示和说明细胞各结构的功能及其相互关系。
指导学生制作临时装片，利用显微镜进行观察，使学生初步学会使用显微镜观察的方法，形成对细胞结构的感性认识。

bio-m-cell-structure-m.name: 细胞的结构
bio-m-cell-structure-m.subject: biology
curriculum_points: 动物细胞、植物细胞都具有细胞膜、细胞质、细胞核等结构。植物细胞具有不同于动物细胞的结构，如叶绿体和细胞壁。
识别动植物细胞的结构并说出其异同点，说明细胞是生物体结构和功能的基本单位。
制作植物细胞、动物细胞的临时装片，用显微镜观察细胞结构；尝试制作植物细胞或动物细胞的结构模型。
chapters: 必修一 第3章

bio-m-circulation-respiration.name: 循环与呼吸综合
bio-m-circulation-respiration.subject: biology
curriculum_points: 人体生理与健康学习主题包括循环系统与呼吸系统等内容，要求学生掌握人体生理与健康的基础知识。
学生应获得人体生理与健康等方面的基础知识，初步形成结构与功能观等生命观念。
树立健康意识和社会责任感，关注身体内外各种因素对健康的影响，形成健康生活的态度和行为习惯。

bio-m-circulatory-system.name: 循环系统
bio-m-circulatory-system.subject: biology
curriculum_points: 人体生理与健康主题包含血液循环系统相关内容，学生应掌握人体生理与健康的基础知识。
学生应能说明血液循环系统等器官系统在维持人体正常生理功能中的作用。
通过观察模型、示意图或视频等，引导学生理解血液循环系统的结构与功能。

bio-m-digestion-system.name: 消化系统
bio-m-digestion-system.subject: biology
curriculum_points: 5. 1 人体通过消化系统从外界获取生命活动所需的营养物质
5.1.1 水、无机盐、糖类、蛋白质、脂质和维生素是人体生命 活动所需的主要营养物质
5.1.2 消化系统由消化道和消化腺组成
chapters: 七年级下册 第4单元 人体生理与健康（一）

bio-m-eco-factors.name: 生态因素
bio-m-eco-factors.subject: biology
curriculum_points: 生态因素能够影响生物的生活和分布，生物能够适应和影响环境
从结构与功能的角度，阐明生态系统中的生产者、消费者、分解者以及非生物环境是一个有机整体
通过资料分析、调查、实验探究等活动，引导学生认识生物与环境的关系
探究影响鼠妇（或蚯蚓等）分布的环境因素，探究植被类型与环境湿度或温度之间的关系

bio-m-endocrine-system-m.name: 内分泌系统
bio-m-endocrine-system-m.subject: biology
curriculum_points: 5. 5.5 甲状腺激素、胰岛素等激素参与人体生命活动的调节 5. 5.6 性激素能促进生殖器官的发育，对第二性征的发育和维 持具有重要作用
5.5.7 人在青春期会出现一些显著的生理变化，如身高和体重 迅速增加、出现第二性征、各项生理功能增强等

bio-m-excretory-system.name: 排泄系统
bio-m-excretory-system.subject: biology
curriculum_points: 概念5 人体通过泌尿系统排出代谢废物，维持内环境的稳定
5.3.1 泌尿系统包括肾脏、输尿管、膀胱和尿道等器官
5.3.2 肾脏是形成尿液的器官，其结构和功能的基本单位是肾单位
5.3.3 尿液的生成和排出过程受神经和激素的调节

bio-m-flower-structure.name: 花的结构与传粉
bio-m-flower-structure.subject: biology
curriculum_points: 概念4 植物有自己的生命周期，可以制造有机物，直接或间接地为其他生物提供食物，参与生物圈的水循环，并维持碳氧平衡。
4.2.1 花是植物的生殖器官，其结构有利于完成传粉和受精。
4.2.2 植物可以通过不同的媒介（如风、昆虫）完成传粉。

curriculum_points: 1.1.A Explain how the properties of water that result from its polarity and hydrogen bonding affect its biological function.

1.1.A.1 Living systems depend on the properties of water to sustain life.
i. Water has polarity, because of the formation of polar covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen within water molecules. This polarity contributes to hydrogen bonding between and within biological molecules.
ii. Water has a high specific heat capacity, which allows for the maintenance of homeostatic body temperature within living organisms.
iii. Water has a high heat of vaporization, which allows for the evaporative cooling of the surrounding environment. In living organisms, this property allows for body temperature to be maintained.
1.1.A.2 The hydrogen bonds between adjacent polar water molecules result in cohesion, adhesion, and surface tension.

biology-ap-macromolecules.name: 生物大分子
biology-ap-macromolecules.subject: biology
biology-ap-macromolecules.domain: Unit 1-2 分子与细胞 Molecular & Cell
curriculum_points:
1.7.A Describe the structure and function of proteins.
1.7.A.1 Proteins comprise linear chains of amino acids connected by the formation of covalent (peptide) bonds that form between a carboxyl group (COOH) of one amino acid and an amine group (NH2) of the next amino acid, resulting in a growing peptide chain.

1.7.A.2 Amino acids are composed of a central carbon atom with a hydrogen atom, a carboxyl group, an amine group, and a variable R group covalently bound to it. The R group of an amino acid can be categorized by three possible chemical properties: hydrophobic/nonpolar, hydrophilic/polar, or ionic. The interactions of these R groups determine the structure and function of that region of the protein.
1.7.A.3 The specific sequence of amino acids in proteins determines the primary structure of a polypeptide as well as the overall shape of the protein.

1.7.A.4 Secondary structures of proteins are made through the local folding that forms from interactions between atoms of the polypeptide backbone of the amino acid chain. Hydrogen bonding forms shapes such as alpha-helices and beta-pleated sheets.
1.7.A.5 The three-dimensional shape of the tertiary structure of a protein results from the formation of hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions, ionic interactions, or disulfide bridges.
1.7.A.6 The quaternary structure arises from interactions between multiple polypeptides. All four levels of a protein structure determine the function of a protein.

biology-ap-water-properties.name: 水的性质
biology-ap-water-properties.subject: biology
biology-ap-water-properties.domain: Unit 1-2 分子与细胞 Molecular & Cell
curriculum_points:
BIG IDEA 1: EVOLUTION
The process of evolution drives the diversity and unity of life. Evolution is a change in the genetic makeup of a population over time, with natural selection as its major driving mechanism. Darwin’s theory, which is supported by evidence from many scientific disciplines, states that inheritable variations occur in individuals in a population. Due to competition for limited resources, individuals with more favorable genetic variations are more likely to survive and produce more offspring, thus passing traits to future generations.

7.2.A.2
Individuals with more favorable phenotypes are more likely to survive and produce more offspring, thus passing traits to subsequent generations.

ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE
7.2.A.3
Evolutionary fitness is measured by reproductive success.

bio-h-ecosystem-stability.name: 生态系统稳定性
bio-h-ecosystem-stability.subject: biology
curriculum_points: 生态系统的稳定性是指生态系统保持或恢复自身结构和功能相对稳定的能力。
阐明生态系统通过自我调节作用抵御和消除一定限度的外来干扰，保持或恢复相对稳定的状态。
举例说明生态系统的稳定性会受到自然或人为因素的影响，如气候变化、人类活动等。

curriculum_points:
BIG IDEA 1: EVOLUTION
The process of evolution drives the diversity and unity of life. Evolution is a change in the genetic makeup of a population over time, with natural selection as its major driving mechanism. Darwin’s theory, which is supported by evidence from many scientific disciplines, states that inheritable variations occur in individuals in a population. Due to competition for limited resources, individuals with more favorable genetic variations are more likely to survive and produce more offspring, thus passing traits to future generations. A diverse gene pool is vital for the survival of species because environmental conditions change. The process of evolution explains the diversity and unity of life, but an explanation about the origin of life is less clear.

Natural selection is a major mechanism of evolution. Natural selection acts on phenotypic variations in populations.

Individuals with more favorable phenotypes are more likely to survive and produce more offspring, thus passing traits to subsequent generations.

TOPIC 7.2 Natural Selection
ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE

biology-ap-cellular-respiration.subject: biology
biology-ap-cellular-respiration.domain: Unit 3-4 细胞能量与通讯 Energy & Communication
curriculum_points:
1.2.A.1
Atoms and molecules from the environment are necessary to build new molecules. Carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen are the most prevalent elements used to build biological molecules such as carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids. Additionally:
i. Sulfur is used in the building of proteins.
ii. Phosphorus is used in the building of phospholipids (a type of lipid) and nucleic acids.
iii. Nitrogen is used in the building of nucleic acids.

1.3.A.1
Hydrolysis is a chemical reaction involving the cleaving of covalent bonds. This type of reaction breaks down molecules into smaller molecules. When water is added to the bond between monomers in a polymer, the bond is broken. The hydrogen ion from a water molecule is added to one monomer and the hydroxyl group of the water molecule is added to the other monomer, completing the reaction.

1.3.A.2
Dehydration synthesis occurs when two smaller molecules are joined together through covalent bonding. A hydrogen ion is removed from one monomer and a hydroxyl group is removed from the other. This causes the loss of the equivalent of a water molecule from the reactants and the connection of the two remaining monomers. The connection of many monomers is known as polymerization.

curriculum_points:
The cell cycle is a highly regulated series of events that controls the growth and reproduction of eukaryotic cells.
i. The cell cycle consists of sequential stages of interphase (G1, S, G2), mitosis, and cytokinesis.
ii. G1 phase: The cell is metabolically active, duplicating organelles and cytosolic components.
iii. S phase: DNA is in the form of chromatin and replicates to form two sister chromatids connected at a centromere.
iv. G2 phase: Protein synthesis occurs, ATP is produced in large quantities, and centrosomes replicate.

Mitosis is a process that ensures the transfer of a complete genome from a parent cell to two genetically identical daughter cells in eukaryotes.
i. Mitosis plays a role in growth, tissue repair, and asexual reproduction.
ii. Mitosis occurs in sequential steps (prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase) and alternates with interphase in the cell cycle.
iii. Prophase: Sister chromatids condense, mitotic spindle begins to form, and centrosomes move to opposite poles of the cell.
iv. Metaphase: Spindle fibers align chromosomes along the equator of the cell.
v. Anaphase: Paired sister chromatids separate as spindle fibers pull chromatids toward poles.
vi. Telophase: Mitotic spindle breaks down, a new nuclear envelope develops, and then the cytoplasm divides.
vii. Cytokinesis: A cleavage furrow forms in animal cells or a cell plate forms in plant cells, resulting in two new daughter cells.
A number of internal controls or checkpoints regulate progression through the cell cycle.
Interactions between cyclins and cyclin-dependent kinases control the cell cycle.

Water has polarity, because of the formation of polar covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen within water molecules. This polarity contributes to hydrogen bonding between and within biological molecules.
The hydrogen bonds between adjacent polar water molecules result in cohesion, adhesion, and surface tension.

biology-ap-population-ecology.subject: biology

curriculum_points: Science Practice 3: Questions and Methods 3: Determine scientific questions and methods. SKILLS: 3.A Identify or pose a testable question based on an observation, data, or a model.

Science Practice 6: Argumentation 6: Develop and justify scientific arguments using evidence. SKILLS: 6.A Make a scientific claim. 6.B Support a claim with evidence from biological principles, concepts, processes, and data. 6.C Provide reasoning to justify a claim by connecting evidence to biological theories.

BIG IDEA 3: INFORMATION STORAGE AND TRANSMISSION: Living systems store, retrieve, transmit, and respond to information essential to life processes. Genetic information provides for continuity of life, and, in most cases, this information is passed from parent to offspring via DNA. Nonheritable information transmission influences behavior within and between cells, organisms, and populations. These behaviors are directed by underlying genetic information, and responses to information are vital to natural selection and evolution. Genetic information is a repository of instructions necessary for the survival, growth, and reproduction of the organism. Genetic variation can be advantageous for the long-term survival and evolution of a species.

UNIT 6: Gene Expression and Regulation: Developing Understanding: Progressing from the continuity of life to gene expression, students gain in-depth knowledge about nucleic acids and their role in gene expression in this unit. There is also a finer focus on the comparison between the structures of DNA and RNA. This unit highlights how an individual’s genotype is physically expressed through their phenotype, thus emphasizing the importance of protein synthesis (transcription and translation) in gene expression. Regulation of gene expression and cell specialization are instrumental in ensuring survival within an individual and across populations.

biology-ap-speciation.name: 物种形成
biology-ap-speciation.subject: biology
biology-ap-speciation.domain: Unit 7-8 进化与生态 Evolution & Ecology
curriculum_points:
BIG IDEA 1: EVOLUTION
The process of evolution drives the diversity and unity of life. Evolution is a change in the genetic makeup of a population over time, with natural selection as its major driving mechanism. Darwin’s theory, which is supported by evidence from many scientific disciplines, states that inheritable variations occur in individuals in a population. Due to competition for limited resources, individuals with more favorable genetic variations are more likely to survive and produce more offspring, thus passing traits to future generations.

7.2 Natural Selection
Explain how natural selection affects populations.
7.2.A.1
Natural selection is a major mechanism of evolution. Natural selection acts on phenotypic variations in populations.
7.2.A.2
Evolution is also driven by random occurrences. Mutations are random and are not directed by environmental or organismal needs. Some mutations are beneficial, increasing the fitness of the organism, while others are harmful, decreasing the fitness of the organism. Mutations are the primary source of new genetic variation in a population.

7.2.A.3
Environments change and apply selective pressures to populations. Evolution occurs when the frequency of alleles in a population changes over time due to natural selection. The unequal survival and reproduction of organisms with different phenotypes, caused by natural selection, can lead to the evolution of populations.

7.2.B
Explain how natural selection affects individuals and populations.
7.2.B.1
Organisms with heritable traits that are better suited to their environment tend to survive and produce more offspring than organisms with less suitable traits. This differential survival and reproduction is the process of natural selection.

chemistry-ap-atomic-structure.name: 原子结构
chemistry-ap-atomic-structure.subject: chemistry
chemistry-ap-atomic-structure.domain: Unit 1-2 原子与化学键 Atoms & Bonding
curriculum_points:
1.5.A  Represent the ground-state electron configuration of an atom of an element or its ions using the Aufbau principle.

ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE
1.5.A.1  The atom is composed of negatively charged electrons and a positively charged nucleus that is made of protons and neutrons.
1.5.A.3  In atoms and ions, the electrons can be thought of as being in “shells (energy levels)” and “subshells (sublevels),” as described by the ground-state electron configuration. Inner electrons are called core electrons, and outer electrons are called valence electrons. The electron configuration is explained by quantum mechanics, as delineated in the Aufbau principle and exemplified in the periodic table of the elements.

1.6.A  Explain the relationship between the photoelectron spectrum of an atom or ion and: i. The ground-state electron configuration of the species. ii. The interactions between the electrons and the nucleus.

ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE
1.6.A.1  The energies of the electrons in a given shell can be measured experimentally with photoelectron spectroscopy (PES). The position of each peak in the PES spectrum is related to the energy required to remove an electron from the corresponding subshell, and the relative height of each peak is (ideally) proportional to the number of electrons in that subshell.

1.7.A  Explain the relationship between trends in atomic properties of elements and electronic structure and periodicity.

ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE
1.7.A.1  The organization of the periodic table is based on patterns of recurring properties of the elements, which are explained by patterns of ground-state electron configurations and the presence of completely or partially filled shells (and subshells) of electrons in atoms.
1.7.A.2  Trends in atomic properties within the periodic table (periodicity) can be predicted by the position of the element on the periodic table and qualitatively understood using Coulomb’s law, the shell model, and the concepts of shielding and effective nuclear charge. These properties include: i. Ionization energy ii. Atomic and ionic radii iii. Electron affinity iv. Electronegativity.

curriculum_points: 1.1.A Calculate quantities of a substance or its relative number of particles using dimensional analysis and the mole concept.

1.1.A.2 Avogadro’s number ( N A = 6.022 × 1 0 23 m o l − 1 ) provides the connection between the number of moles in a pure sample of a substance and the number of constituent particles (or formula units) of that substance.

1.1.A.3 Expressing the mass of an individual atom or molecule in atomic mass units (amu) is useful because the average mass in amu of one particle (atom or molecule) or formula unit of a substance will always be numerically equal to the molar mass of that substance in grams. Thus, there is a quantitative connection between the mass of a substance and the number of particles that the substance contains.

chem-cam-al-alcohols-esters.subject: chemistry
curriculum_points:
1.3 Electrons, energy levels and atomic orbitals
In 1.3 each atom or ion described will be in the ground state. Only the elements hydrogen to krypton will be assessed.
Learning outcomes
Candidates should be able to:
1 understand the terms:
• shells, sub-shells and orbitals
• principal quantum number (n)
• ground state, limited to electronic configuration
2 describe the number of orbitals making up s, p and d sub-shells, and the number of electrons that can fill s, p and d sub-shells
3 describe the order of increasing energy of the sub-shells within the first three shells and the 4s and 4p sub-shells
4 describe the electronic configurations to include the number of electrons in each shell, sub-shell and orbital
5 explain the electronic configurations in terms of energy of the electrons and inter-electron repulsion
6 determine the electronic configuration of atoms and ions given the atomic or proton number and charge, using either of the following conventions:
e.g. for Fe: 1s22s22p63s23p63d64s2 (full electronic configuration)
or [Ar] 3d64s2 (shorthand electronic configuration)
7 understand and use the electrons in boxes notation
e.g. for Fe: [Ar]
8 describe and sketch the shapes of s and p orbitals
9 describe a free radical as a species with one or more unpaired electrons

1.4 Ionisation energy
In 1.4 each atom or ion described will be in the ground state. Only the elements hydrogen to krypton will be assessed.
Learning outcomes
Candidates should be able to:
1 define and use the term first ionisation energy, IE
2 construct equations to represent first, second and subsequent ionisation energies
3 identify and explain the trends in ionisation energies across a period and down a group of the Periodic Table
4 identify and explain the variation in successive ionisation energies of an element
5 understand that ionisation energies are due to the attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron
6 explain the factors influencing the ionisation energies of elements in terms of nuclear charge, atomic/ionic radius, shielding by inner shells and sub-shells and spin-pair repulsion
7 deduce the electronic configurations of elements using successive ionisation energy data
8 deduce the position of an element in the Periodic Table using successive ionisation energy data

curriculum_points: 1.5.A Represent the ground-state electron configuration of an atom of an element or its ions using the Aufbau principle.
1.5.A.2 Coulomb’s law is used to calculate the force between two charged particles.

1.5.A.3 In atoms and ions, the electrons can be thought of as being in “shells (energy levels)” and “subshells (sublevels),” as described by the ground-state electron configuration. Inner electrons are called core electrons, and outer electrons are called valence electrons. The electron configuration is explained by quantum mechanics, as delineated in the Aufbau principle and exemplified in the periodic table of the elements.

1.5.A.4 The relative energy required to remove an electron from different subshells of an atom or ion or from the same subshell in different atoms or ions (ionization energy) can be estimated through a qualitative application of Coulomb’s law. This energy is related to the distance from the nucleus and the effective (shield) charge of the nucleus.

1.7.A.2
Trends in atomic properties within the periodic table (periodicity) can be predicted by the position of the element on the periodic table and qualitatively understood using Coulomb’s law, the shell model, and the concepts of shielding and effective nuclear charge. These properties include:
i. Ionization energy
ii. Atomic and ionic radii
iii. Electron affinity
iv. Electronegativity.

1.7.A.1
The organization of the periodic table is based on patterns of recurring properties of the elements, which are explained by patterns of ground-state electron configurations and the presence of completely or partially filled shells (and subshells) of electrons in atoms.

1.7.A.3
The periodicity (in 1.7.A.2) is useful to predict/estimate values of properties in the absence of data.

chemistry-ap-enthalpy.name: 焓变
chemistry-ap-enthalpy.subject: chemistry
chemistry-ap-enthalpy.domain: Unit 5-6 动力学与热力学 Kinetics & Thermodynamics
curriculum_points:
5.1.A.1
The kinetics of a chemical reaction is defined as the rate at which an amount of reactants is converted to products per unit of time.

5.1.A.3
The rate of a reaction is influenced by reactant concentrations, temperature, surface area, catalysts, and other environmental factors.

5.5.A.1
For an elementary reaction to successfully produce products, reactants must successfully collide to initiate bond-breaking and bond-making events.

5.5.A.2
In most reactions, only a small fraction of the collisions leads to a reaction. Successful collisions have both sufficient energy to overcome the activation energy requirements and orientations that allow the bonds to rearrange in the required manner.

Practice 2 Question and Method
SKILLS
2.A Identify a testable scientific question based on an observation, data, or a model.
2.B Formulate a hypothesis or predict the results of an experiment.

2.D Make observations or collect data from representations of laboratory setups or results, while attending to precision where appropriate.
2.E Identify or describe potential sources of experimental error.
2.F Explain how modifications to an experimental procedure will alter results.

Practice 3 Representing Data and Phenomena 3
Create representations or models of chemical phenomena.
SKILLS
3.A Represent chemical phenomena using appropriate graphing techniques, including correct scale and units.
3.B Represent chemical substances or phenomena with appropriate diagrams or models (e.g., electron configuration).

Develop an explanation or scientific argument.

6.E Provide reasoning to justify a claim using connections between particulate and macroscopic scales or levels.

1.3 Electrons, energy levels and atomic orbitals
In 1.3 each atom or ion described will be in the ground state. Only the elements hydrogen to krypton will be assessed.
Learning outcomes
Candidates should be able to:
1 understand the terms:
• shells, sub-shells and orbitals
• principal quantum number (n)
• ground state, limited to electronic configuration
2 describe the number of orbitals making up s, p and d sub-shells, and the number of electrons that can fill s, p and d sub-shells

7 understand and use the electrons in boxes notation

7 deduce the electronic configurations of elements using successive ionisation energy data
8 deduce the position of an element in the Periodic Table using successive ionisation energy data

1.3.C.2
The arithmetic operators consist of addition +, subtraction -, multiplication *, division /, and remainder %. An arithmetic operation that uses two int values will evaluate to an int value. An arithmetic operation that uses at least one double value will evaluate to a double value.

1.3.C.5
Operators can be used to construct compound expressions. At compile time, numeric values are associated with operators according to operator precedence to determine how they are grouped. Parentheses can be used to modify operator precedence. Multiplication, division, and remainder have precedence over addition and subtraction. Operators with the same precedence are evaluated from left to right.

1.3.C.3
When dividing numeric values that are both int values, the result is only the integer portion of the quotient. When dividing numeric values that use at least one double value, the result is the quotient.

1.3.C.4
The remainder operator % is used to compute the remainder when one number a is divided by another number b.

design-ib-myp-myp-inquire-analyse.name: 探究与分析
design-ib-myp-myp-inquire-analyse.subject: design
design-ib-myp-myp-inquire-analyse.domain: 设计循环 / Design Cycle / Design Cycle
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to formulate a detailed design brief by identifying and analysing a need for a specific client or target audience.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to conduct and synthesize research from a range of primary and secondary sources to inform the development of a design specification.

design-ib-myp-myp-develop-ideas.name: 构思与方案
design-ib-myp-myp-develop-ideas.subject: design
design-ib-myp-myp-develop-ideas.domain: 设计循环 / Design Cycle / Design Cycle
curriculum_points: Students will be able to generate a range of feasible design ideas, using techniques such as annotation and sketching, that address the specifications outlined in the design brief.
Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to develop detailed planning drawings/diagrams and justify the selection of one final design against the specification.

design-ib-myp-myp-sketching.name: 设计草图
design-ib-myp-myp-sketching.subject: design
design-ib-myp-myp-sketching.domain: 产品设计 / Product Design / Product Design
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to use freehand sketching techniques, including annotation, to communicate design ideas and explore form.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to produce annotated, rendered sketches that effectively communicate aesthetic and functional details of a proposed solution.

design-ib-myp-myp-create-solution.name: 制作解决方案
design-ib-myp-myp-create-solution.subject: design
design-ib-myp-myp-create-solution.domain: 设计循环 / Design Cycle / Design Cycle
curriculum_points: Students will be able to competently use a range of techniques and equipment to construct a logical plan and create a high-quality prototype or product.
Students in MYP 2-5 will demonstrate technical skill and safety in the use of tools and materials, documenting the creation process with photographic evidence.

design-ib-myp-myp-materials-tools.name: 材料与工具
design-ib-myp-myp-materials-tools.subject: design
design-ib-myp-myp-materials-tools.domain: 产品设计 / Product Design / Product Design
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to identify and describe the working properties of common materials (e.g., wood, polymers, textiles) and select appropriate tools for basic processing.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to justify their selection of specific materials, components, and tools based on functional requirements, availability, cost, and environmental impact.

design-ib-myp-myp-programming-intro.name: 编程入门
design-ib-myp-myp-programming-intro.subject: design
design-ib-myp-myp-programming-intro.domain: 数字设计 / Digital Design / Digital Design
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to use visual or text-based programming environments to create simple algorithms that solve defined problems, using constructs such as sequences, loops, and conditionals.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to design, write, debug, and document a functional program to address a specific need within a design project.

design-ib-myp-myp-user-research.name: 用户研究
design-ib-myp-myp-user-research.subject: design
design-ib-myp-myp-user-research.domain: 研究与评估 / Research & Evaluation / Research & Evaluation
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to use simple methods (e.g., surveys, interviews, observation) to gather information about user needs and preferences.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to synthesize findings from user research to create detailed user personas and scenarios that drive the design specification.

design-ib-myp-myp-design-specs.name: 设计规范书
design-ib-myp-myp-design-specs.subject: design
design-ib-myp-myp-design-specs.domain: 研究与评估 / Research & Evaluation / Research & Evaluation
curriculum_points: Students will be able to develop a design specification with a list of clear, measurable criteria derived from the analysis of their design brief and research.
Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to prioritize specification criteria and justify how they address the needs of the client and the requirements of the problem.

design-ib-myp-myp-evaluate.name: 评估与迭代
design-ib-myp-myp-evaluate.subject: design
design-ib-myp-myp-evaluate.domain: 设计循环 / Design Cycle / Design Cycle
curriculum_points: Students will be able to test their final product/solution against the original design specification and explain the success and limitations of the outcome.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to critically evaluate the impact of their solution on the client/target audience and propose detailed, realistic modifications for improvement.

design-ib-myp-myp-prototyping.name: 原型制作
design-ib-myp-myp-prototyping.subject: design
design-ib-myp-myp-prototyping.domain: 产品设计 / Product Design / Product Design
curriculum_points: Students will be able to construct a physical or digital prototype that models key features of their final design idea for the purpose of testing and evaluation.
Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to select and justify appropriate prototyping methods (e.g., paper, 3D print, digital mock-up) based on the design context and testing goals.

design-ib-myp-myp-web-basics.name: 网页基础（HTML/CSS）
design-ib-myp-myp-web-basics.subject: design
design-ib-myp-myp-web-basics.domain: 数字设计 / Digital Design / Digital Design
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to explain the core components of web architecture (e.g., HTML, CSS, servers) and create a simple, functional multi-page website using basic tags and styling.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to design and develop a website that follows principles of user-centered design and digital accessibility.

design-ib-myp-myp-cad-basics.name: CAD 入门
design-ib-myp-myp-cad-basics.subject: design
design-ib-myp-myp-cad-basics.domain: 产品设计 / Product Design / Product Design
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 2-4 will be able to use basic CAD software tools to create and modify simple 2D drawings and 3D digital models.
Students in MYP 5 will be able to produce a set of annotated CAD drawings suitable for guiding the manufacture of a prototype, applying scale and dimensioning conventions.

design-ib-myp-myp-ethics-sustainability.name: 伦理与可持续
design-ib-myp-myp-ethics-sustainability.subject: design
design-ib-myp-myp-ethics-sustainability.domain: 研究与评估 / Research & Evaluation / Research & Evaluation
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 1-3 will be able to identify ethical and environmental considerations (e.g., sourcing, waste, inclusivity) relevant to a design context.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to critically evaluate a design solution's social and environmental impact and propose modifications that align with principles of sustainable design.

design-ib-myp-myp-ui-design.name: 用户界面设计
design-ib-myp-myp-ui-design.subject: design
design-ib-myp-myp-ui-design.domain: 数字设计 / Digital Design / Digital Design
curriculum_points: Students will be able to apply fundamental principles of user interface design (e.g., consistency, hierarchy, feedback) to develop low-fidelity wireframes for a digital product.
Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to justify their UI design choices in relation to the needs and characteristics of a specific user group.

design-ib-myp-myp-user-testing.name: 用户测试
design-ib-myp-myp-user-testing.subject: design
design-ib-myp-myp-user-testing.domain: 数字设计 / Digital Design / Digital Design
curriculum_points: Students will be able to plan and conduct simple user tests to gather qualitative and quantitative feedback on a prototype.
Students in MYP 4-5 will be able to analyse user testing data, identify patterns, and translate findings into specific design modifications.

economics-ib-dp-dp-demand-supply.name: 供求分析
economics-ib-dp-dp-demand-supply.subject: economics
curriculum_points: Students will be able to construct and analyse demand and supply diagrams to illustrate market equilibrium, and explain the causes and consequences of shifts in and movements along these curves.
Students will be able to apply the model of demand and supply to real-world markets, explaining how the price mechanism allocates resources and rations goods.

economics-ib-dp-dp-efficiency-equity.name: 效率与公平
economics-ib-dp-dp-efficiency-equity.subject: economics
economics-ib-dp-dp-efficiency-equity.domain: 关键概念 / Key Concepts / Key Concepts
curriculum_points: Students will be able to distinguish between allocative, productive, and dynamic efficiency and explain the trade-off between equity and efficiency in economic policy.
Students will be able to evaluate government policies, such as progressive taxation and transfer payments, aimed at promoting greater equity (fairness) in the distribution of income and wealth.

economics-ib-dp-dp-elasticity.name: 弹性
economics-ib-dp-dp-elasticity.subject: economics
curriculum_points: Students will be able to calculate and interpret price elasticity of demand (PED), price elasticity of supply (PES), income elasticity of demand (YED), and cross-price elasticity of demand (XED).
Students will be able to evaluate the significance of elasticity for stakeholders, including consumers, producers, and governments, in areas such as tax incidence and revenue.

economics-ib-dp-dp-gdp.name: GDP 与国民收入
economics-ib-dp-dp-gdp.subject: economics
curriculum_points: Students will be able to explain the circular flow of income model and calculate nominal and real GDP using the expenditure, income, and output methods.
Students will be able to evaluate the uses and limitations of GDP statistics as a measure of economic well-being and standard of living.

economics-ib-dp-dp-scarcity-choice.name: 稀缺与选择
economics-ib-dp-dp-scarcity-choice.subject: economics
curriculum_points: Students will be able to explain the central economic problem of scarcity, choice, and opportunity cost, using production possibility curve (PPC) models to illustrate these concepts.
Students will be able to evaluate the trade-offs and opportunity costs involved in economic decision-making by individuals, firms, and governments.

economics-ib-dp-dp-ad-as.name: AD-AS 模型
economics-ib-dp-dp-ad-as.subject: economics
curriculum_points: Students will be able to construct and interpret the aggregate demand (AD) and aggregate supply (AS) model to illustrate macroeconomic equilibrium, the business cycle, and inflationary/deflationary gaps.
Students will be able to analyse the causes of shifts in the AD and AS curves and evaluate their impacts on the price level, real output, and employment.

economics-ib-dp-dp-balance-payments.name: 国际收支
economics-ib-dp-dp-balance-payments.subject: economics
economics-ib-dp-dp-balance-payments.domain: 全球经济 / Global Economy / Global Economy
curriculum_points: Students will be able to explain the structure of the balance of payments accounts, distinguishing between the current account and the capital/financial account.
Students will be able to analyse the causes and consequences of current account deficits and surpluses, and evaluate policy responses to address imbalances.

economics-ib-dp-dp-development-econ.name: 发展经济学
economics-ib-dp-dp-development-econ.subject: economics
economics-ib-dp-dp-development-econ.domain: 全球经济 / Global Economy / Global Economy
curriculum_points: Students will be able to compare and contrast alternative measures of economic development, including the Human Development Index (HDI) and the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI).
Students will be able to evaluate the role of domestic factors (e.g., education, institutional quality) and international factors (e.g., debt, aid, trade) in economic development.

economics-ib-dp-dp-economic-growth.name: 经济增长
economics-ib-dp-dp-economic-growth.subject: economics
curriculum_points: Students will be able to distinguish between economic growth (an increase in real GDP) and economic development (broader improvements in living standards).

Students will be able to analyse the sources of long-term economic growth (increases in quantity/quality of factors of production, technological advances) and evaluate its potential consequences, including environmental impacts.

economics-ib-dp-dp-economic-integration.name: 经济一体化
economics-ib-dp-dp-economic-integration.subject: economics
economics-ib-dp-dp-economic-integration.domain: 全球经济 / Global Economy / Global Economy
curriculum_points: Students will be able to explain the different forms of economic integration, from preferential trade agreements to monetary unions, using real-world examples.
Students will be able to evaluate the potential economic benefits (e.g., trade creation) and costs (e.g., trade diversion, loss of sovereignty) of regional economic integration.

economics-ib-dp-dp-exchange-rates.name: 汇率
economics-ib-dp-dp-exchange-rates.subject: economics
economics-ib-dp-dp-exchange-rates.domain: 全球经济 / Global Economy / Global Economy
curriculum_points: Students will be able to distinguish between floating, fixed, and managed exchange rate systems and illustrate how they are determined in a foreign exchange market diagram.
Students will be able to analyse the causes and consequences of exchange rate fluctuations for a nation's inflation, unemployment, current account balance, and economic growth.

economics-ib-dp-dp-firm-theory-hl.name: 厂商理论（HL）
economics-ib-dp-dp-firm-theory-hl.subject: economics
curriculum_points: HL students will be able to calculate and interpret revenue, cost, and profit data for firms in different market structures (perfect competition, monopoly, monopolistic competition).
HL students will be able to diagrammatically analyse short-run and long-run equilibrium positions for profit-maximizing firms and evaluate the efficiency outcomes of different market structures.

economics-ib-dp-dp-fiscal-monetary.name: 财政与货币政策
economics-ib-dp-dp-fiscal-monetary.subject: economics
curriculum_points: Students will be able to explain how expansionary and contractionary fiscal policy (changes in government spending and taxation) and monetary policy (changes in interest rates) can be used to influence aggregate demand.
Students will be able to evaluate the effectiveness, strengths, and limitations of demand-side policies in achieving macroeconomic objectives such as low unemployment and price stability.

economics-ib-dp-dp-govt-intervention.name: 政府干预
economics-ib-dp-dp-govt-intervention.subject: economics
curriculum_points: Students will be able to evaluate the use of government intervention methods, including indirect taxes, subsidies, tradable permits, and direct provision, to correct market failures.
Students will be able to analyse the consequences of government intervention, including price ceilings and price floors, on market outcomes, stakeholders, and government budgets.

economics-ib-dp-dp-inequality.name: 不平等
economics-ib-dp-dp-inequality.subject: economics
economics-ib-dp-dp-inequality.domain: 关键概念 / Key Concepts / Key Concepts
curriculum_points: Students will be able to analyse the causes of income and wealth inequality within and between countries using tools such as the Lorenz curve and Gini coefficient.
Students will be able to evaluate the economic and social impacts of inequality and assess the effectiveness of policies designed to reduce it.

economics-ib-dp-dp-inflation.name: 通货膨胀
economics-ib-dp-dp-inflation.subject: economics
curriculum_points: Students will be able to distinguish between demand-pull and cost-push inflation using AD/AS analysis and calculate inflation rates from a set of price index data.
Students will be able to evaluate the consequences of inflation and deflation for consumers, firms, the government, and the economy as a whole.

economics-ib-dp-dp-intl-trade.name: 国际贸易
economics-ib-dp-dp-intl-trade.subject: economics
economics-ib-dp-dp-intl-trade.domain: 全球经济 / Global Economy / Global Economy
curriculum_points: Students will be able to explain the theory of comparative advantage and illustrate the potential gains from trade and specialization using diagrams.
Students will be able to analyse the arguments for and against trade protectionism (tariffs, quotas, subsidies) and evaluate their impacts on stakeholders.

economics-ib-dp-dp-market-failure.name: 市场失灵
economics-ib-dp-dp-market-failure.subject: economics
curriculum_points: Students will be able to explain, with examples, the concepts of negative externalities, positive externalities, common pool resources, and public goods as sources of market failure.
Students will be able to illustrate market failure using marginal social benefit (MSB) and marginal social cost (MSC) diagrams, identifying the welfare loss.

economics-ib-dp-dp-sustainability-econ.name: 可持续性
economics-ib-dp-dp-sustainability-econ.subject: economics
economics-ib-dp-dp-sustainability-econ.domain: 关键概念 / Key Concepts / Key Concepts
curriculum_points: Students will be able to explain the concept of sustainable development and evaluate the role of market-based (e.g., carbon taxes) and government-led strategies in promoting environmental sustainability.
Students will be able to critically assess the potential conflict between the macroeconomic objectives of economic growth and environmental sustainability.

economics-ib-dp-dp-unemployment.name: 失业
economics-ib-dp-dp-unemployment.subject: economics
curriculum_points: Students will be able to distinguish between the main types of unemployment (frictional, structural, cyclical, seasonal) and explain their causes.
Students will be able to calculate the unemployment rate and evaluate the economic and social consequences of unemployment for different stakeholders.

ee-ib-dp-dp-choose-subject.name: 选题与学科
ee-ib-dp-dp-choose-subject.subject: ee
ee-ib-dp-dp-choose-subject.domain: 研究设计 / Research Design / Research Design
curriculum_points: Students will be able to select an appropriate Diploma Programme subject for their Extended Essay, ensuring it aligns with their academic interests and the subject's availability within the IB framework.
Students will justify their subject choice by demonstrating a clear understanding of the subject's disciplinary conventions and its suitability for a 4000-word independent investigation.

ee-ib-dp-dp-first-reflection.name: 初次反思
ee-ib-dp-dp-first-reflection.subject: ee
ee-ib-dp-dp-first-reflection.domain: 反思与面谈 / Reflection & RPPF / Reflection & RPPF
curriculum_points: Students will complete the first reflection session on the Reflections on planning and progress form (RPPF), reflecting on their initial ideas, the formulation of their research question, and their planning process.

ee-ib-dp-dp-literature-review.name: 文献综述
ee-ib-dp-dp-literature-review.subject: ee
ee-ib-dp-dp-literature-review.domain: 研究设计 / Research Design / Research Design
curriculum_points: Students will conduct a comprehensive review of relevant scholarly literature, situating their research question within the existing academic discourse of the field.
Students will synthesize and critically evaluate the literature, identifying gaps, debates, or contexts that their own investigation will address.

ee-ib-dp-dp-research-methodology.name: 研究方法
ee-ib-dp-dp-research-methodology.subject: ee
ee-ib-dp-dp-research-methodology.domain: 研究设计 / Research Design / Research Design
curriculum_points: Students will design and justify a coherent research methodology appropriate to their subject and research question, demonstrating an understanding of primary and/or secondary research methods.
Students will apply their chosen methodology systematically, explaining its application and acknowledging any limitations in their research process.

ee-ib-dp-dp-research-question.name: 研究问题（RQ）
ee-ib-dp-dp-research-question.subject: ee
ee-ib-dp-dp-research-question.domain: 研究设计 / Research Design / Research Design
curriculum_points: Students will formulate a clear, focused, and arguable research question that is appropriate for an in-depth, 4000-word academic investigation within their chosen subject.
Students will refine their initial research question through preliminary reading to ensure it is manageable, specific, and conducive to critical analysis and argument.

ee-ib-dp-dp-argument-analysis.name: 论证与分析
ee-ib-dp-dp-argument-analysis.subject: ee
ee-ib-dp-dp-argument-analysis.domain: 写作阶段 / Writing Process / Writing Process
curriculum_points: Students will develop a sustained, reasoned argument in response to their research question, supported by critical analysis of evidence.
Students will demonstrate higher-order thinking skills by evaluating different perspectives, interpreting data or sources, and drawing well-substantiated conclusions.

ee-ib-dp-dp-citations.name: 引用规范（MLA/APA）
ee-ib-dp-dp-citations.subject: ee
ee-ib-dp-dp-citations.domain: 写作阶段 / Writing Process / Writing Process
curriculum_points: Students will consistently and accurately apply a recognized system of academic referencing (e.g., MLA, APA, Chicago) to acknowledge all sources used in their work.
Students will understand and avoid academic misconduct by distinguishing between their own ideas and those of others through proper paraphrasing, quoting, and citation.

ee-ib-dp-dp-ee-humanities.name: 文科 EE 要点
ee-ib-dp-dp-ee-humanities.subject: ee
ee-ib-dp-dp-ee-humanities.domain: 学科差异 / Subject-Specific Tips / Subject-Specific
curriculum_points: Students undertaking a Humanities EE (e.g., History, Economics, Psychology) will construct a critical argument based on the systematic analysis and evaluation of primary and secondary sources.
Students will demonstrate an understanding of the theoretical frameworks and historiographical or disciplinary debates relevant to their chosen topic.

ee-ib-dp-dp-ee-math.name: 数学 EE 要点
ee-ib-dp-dp-ee-math.subject: ee
ee-ib-dp-dp-ee-math.domain: 学科差异 / Subject-Specific Tips / Subject-Specific
curriculum_points: Students undertaking a Mathematics EE will engage in the exploration of a specific mathematical topic, demonstrating rigorous and precise mathematical reasoning and communication.
The essay may involve applying mathematics to solve a problem, proving theorems, or analyzing mathematical models, with a clear emphasis on the beauty and utility of mathematics itself.

ee-ib-dp-dp-ee-sciences.name: 理科 EE 要点
ee-ib-dp-dp-ee-sciences.subject: ee
ee-ib-dp-dp-ee-sciences.domain: 学科差异 / Subject-Specific Tips / Subject-Specific
curriculum_points: Students undertaking a Science EE will design and conduct a safe and ethically sound investigation, collecting and processing primary or secondary data to explore a specific scientific question.
Students will analyze their results using appropriate scientific methods and techniques, discussing their significance in relation to established scientific theory and the research question.

ee-ib-dp-dp-ee-world-studies.name: 世界研究 EE
ee-ib-dp-dp-ee-world-studies.subject: ee
ee-ib-dp-dp-ee-world-studies.domain: 学科差异 / Subject-Specific Tips / Subject-Specific
curriculum_points: Students undertaking a World Studies EE will formulate a research question of contemporary global significance that examines an issue through the lens of at least two IB disciplines.
Students will integrate concepts, theories, and methods from their chosen disciplines to construct a coherent interdisciplinary analysis of the complex global issue.

ee-ib-dp-dp-formatting.name: 格式规范
ee-ib-dp-dp-formatting.subject: ee
ee-ib-dp-dp-formatting.domain: 写作阶段 / Writing Process / Writing Process
curriculum_points: Students will adhere to the formal presentation requirements for the Extended Essay, including title page, abstract, contents page, page numbering, and overall layout as specified in the EE guide.
Students will ensure their final submission is professionally presented and meets the technical requirements for assessment.

ee-ib-dp-dp-interim-reflection.name: 中期反思
ee-ib-dp-dp-interim-reflection.subject: ee
ee-ib-dp-dp-interim-reflection.domain: 反思与面谈 / Reflection & RPPF / Reflection & RPPF
curriculum_points: Students will complete the interim reflection on the RPPF, evaluating the progress of their research and writing, discussing challenges encountered, and outlining their plan for completion.

ee-ib-dp-dp-outline-structure.name: 大纲与结构
ee-ib-dp-dp-outline-structure.subject: ee
ee-ib-dp-dp-outline-structure.domain: 写作阶段 / Writing Process / Writing Process
curriculum_points: Students will construct a logical and coherent outline for their essay, ensuring the structure effectively supports the development of their argument and analysis.
Students will organize their essay according to the formal conventions of academic writing in their subject area, including a clear introduction, development, and conclusion.

ee-ib-dp-dp-rppf.name: RPPF 反思表
ee-ib-dp-dp-rppf.subject: ee
ee-ib-dp-dp-rppf.domain: 反思与面谈 / Reflection & RPPF / Reflection & RPPF
curriculum_points: Students will complete all three mandatory reflections on the official RPPF, using the form to document their engagement with the research process and their intellectual and personal development.

ee-ib-dp-dp-viva-voce.name: 终审面谈
ee-ib-dp-dp-viva-voce.subject: ee
ee-ib-dp-dp-viva-voce.domain: 反思与面谈 / Reflection & RPPF / Reflection & RPPF
curriculum_points: Following the completion of the Extended Essay, students will participate in a concluding interview (viva voce) with their supervisor to reflect on their learning journey, the research process, and the outcomes of their work.

Stage 4 Reading: Vocabulary and language: Read and understand a range of words using knowledge of morphology and etymology, e.g. word roots and families, prefixes and suffixes.

english-us-k5-print-concepts.name: 印刷概念

curriculum_points: 1. With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text. 2. With prompting and support, retell familiar stories, including key details. 3. With prompting and support, identify characters, settings, and major events in a story.

Capitalize the first word in a sentence and the pronoun I. b. Recognize and name end punctuation. c. Write a letter or letters for most consonant and short-vowel sounds (phonemes). d. Spell simple words phonetically, drawing on knowledge of sound-letter relationships.

english-us-hs-informative-hs.name: 说明文写作
english-us-hs-informative-hs.subject: english
curriculum_points: WHST.11-12.2 Write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/ experiments, or technical processes. a. Introduce a topic and organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension. b. Develop the topic thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience’s knowledge of the topic. c. Use varied transitions and sentence structures to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts. d. Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary and techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic; convey a knowledgeable stance in a style that responds to the discipline and context as well as to the expertise of likely readers. e. Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation provided (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

curriculum_points: RL.11-12.1: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

RL.11-12.2: Determine two or more themes or central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to produce a complex account; provide an objective summary of the text.

RL.11-12.3: Analyze the impact of the author’s choices regarding how to develop and relate elements of a story or drama (e.g., where a story is set, how the action is ordered, how the characters are introduced and developed).

RL.11-12.5: Analyze how an author’s choices concerning how to structure specific parts of a text (e.g., the choice of where to begin or end a story, the choice to provide a comedic or tragic resolution) contribute to its overall structure and meaning as well as its aesthetic impact.
RL.11-12.6: Analyze a case in which grasping a point of view requires distinguishing what is directly stated in a text from what is really meant (e.g., satire, sarcasm, irony, or understatement).

curriculum_points:
The key concepts for Cambridge International AS & A Level Literature in English are:
• Language
Exploring the variety and use of language in literary texts. Identifying literary techniques and explaining how their use contributes to a reader’s analysis and understanding of the text.
• Form
Considering the ways in which writers use – or depart from – conventions of literary forms of prose, poetry and drama and how those inform meaning and effects.
• Structure
When analysed in reading: the organisation of a text or passage, its shape and development and how this contributes to the readers’ understanding of its meaning and effects.
When used in writing: the construction of a relevant and supported argument appropriate to the question.

The assessment objectives (AOs) are:
AO1 Knowledge and understanding
Respond with understanding to literary texts in a variety of forms, from different cultures; with an appreciation of relevant contexts that illuminate readings of the texts.
AO2 Analysis
Analyse ways in which writers’ choices of language, form and structure shape meanings and effects.

Throughout the AS and A Level course learners will be encouraged to practise their skills in close reading through the study of literary extracts and unseen texts; developing skills of analysis and interpretation of texts, alongside their expression of personal response to the texts studied. Learners will explore the conventions of genres of texts and the contexts in which works have been written, read and received.

AO4 Communication Communicate a relevant, structured and supported response appropriate to literary study.

In response to unseen texts, considering the ways in which a text’s meaning is shaped by conventions of form alongside those of language and style. • Style Analysing the ways in which choices regarding form, structure and language interact to create a distinctive style, for different forms and genres. • Interpretation At AS Level: Evaluating and explaining different ideas within a text. At A Level: Evaluating and explaining different ideas within a text and using different critical readings to explore an understanding of texts and to help support literary arguments.

Throughout the AS and A Level course learners will be encouraged to practise their skills in close reading through the study of literary extracts and unseen texts; developing skills of analysis and interpretation of texts, alongside their expression of personal response to the texts studied. curriculum_points: The aims are to enable students to: • develop an appreciation of and an informed personal response to literature in English in a range of texts in different forms, and from different periods and cultures • analyse and evaluate the methods writers use in creating meaning and effects

The key concepts for Cambridge International AS & A Level Literature in English are: • Language Exploring the variety and use of language in literary texts. Identifying literary techniques and explaining how their use contributes to a reader’s analysis and understanding of the text. • Form Considering the ways in which writers use – or depart from – conventions of literary forms of prose, poetry and drama and how those inform meaning and effects. • Structure When analysed in reading: the organisation of a text or passage, its shape and development and how this contributes to the readers’ understanding of its meaning and effects.
The assessment objectives (AOs) are: AO2 Analysis Analyse ways in which writers’ choices of language, form and structure shape meanings and effects.
Candidates must demonstrate the following: • analysis of the ways in which writers’ choices shape meaning and create effects

hist-m-spring-autumn-warring.name: 春秋战国
hist-m-spring-autumn-warring.subject: history

curriculum_points:
KC-5.3.II.i
Reconstruction and the Civil War ended slavery, altered relationships between the states and the federal government, and led to debates over new definitions of citizenship, particularly regarding the rights of African Americans, women, and other minorities.

KC-5.3.II.A
The 13th Amendment abolished slavery, while the 14th and 15th amendments granted African Americans citizenship, equal protection under the laws, and voting rights.

KC-5.3.II.C
Efforts by radical and moderate Republicans to change the balance of power between Congress and the presidency and to reorder race relations in the defeated South yielded some short-term successes. Reconstruction opened up political opportunities and other leadership roles to former slaves, but it ultimately failed, due both to determined Southern resistance and the North’s waning resolve.

KC-5.3.II.E
Segregation, violence, Supreme Court decisions, and local political tactics progressively stripped away African American rights, but the 14th and 15th amendments eventually became the basis for court decisions upholding civil rights in the 20th century.

Reconstruction opened up political opportunities and other leadership roles to former slaves, but it ultimately failed, due both to determined Southern resistance and the North’s waning resolve.

KC-5.3.II.E
Segregation, violence, Supreme Court decisions, and local political tactics progressively stripped away African American rights, but the 14th and 15th amendments eventually became the basis for court decisions upholding civil rights in the 20th century.

hist-h-reform-comparison.name: 中外改革比较
hist-h-reform-comparison.subject: history
curriculum_points: （二）选择性必修课程模块1 国家制度与社会治理【内容要求】 本课程通过国家制度和社会治理的相关内容，揭示人类政治生活 的发展。本课程由6 个专题组成，是在必修课程基础上的递进与 拓展。 人类社会进入文明时代的一个重要标志是国家的产生，国家统治 依赖一系列制度建设，包括建立组织和制定规则。以权力分配、机构 设置和运行为主的政治体制，规定了国家制度的基本框架。人事管 理、法律、外交、财政都是国家制度不可或缺的重要组成部分，社会 治理则是国家关注的重点。自古及今，东西方各国的制度建设和社会 治理经历了漫长而曲折的发展历程，中国也发生过多次变法与改革， 积累了丰富的经验和深刻的教训，不能脱离特定社会政治条件和历史 文化传统来抽象评判。学习这些内容，加深学生运用唯物史观的阶级 --- 分析方法，对上层建筑的各领域的实质进行深入分析，认识国家治理 体系和治理能力现代化的重要性。 1.1 政治体制 了解中国古代政治体制在秦朝建立前后的巨大变化；通过宰相制 度和地方行政层级管理的变化，认识自秦起君主专制中央集权政治体 制的演变线索；了解古代至近代西方政治体制各主要类型的产生和演 变过程，以及共和制在中国建立的曲折过程，理解中国政治道路发展 的独特性。 1.2 官员的选拔与管理 了解中国古代官员选拔方式的更迭过程和不同阶段的特征，知道 中央集权体制下古代中国的官员考核和监察制度；了解中国科举制与 西方近代文官制度渊源关系，知道西方近代文官制度的特点，以及对 近现代中国公务员制度的影响。 1.3 法律与教化 知道中国先秦时期成文法的产生过程，以及这一时期思想家对于 德治、法治关系的讨论；知道自西汉起历代王朝法律、礼教并用的统 治手段；了解近代西方法律制度的渊源和基本特征，知道宗教伦理在 西方社会发展进程中的作用；了解当代中国的法制建设和精神文明建 设成就。 1.4 民族关系与国家关系 了解中国古代的民族政策和边疆管理制度，认识中国作为统一多 民族国家的发展历程，以及中国古代处理对外关系的体制；了解近代 西方民族国家的形成情况，以及国际法的发展；了解当代中国民族区 域自治制度的历史意义，以及独立自主的和平外交政策的主要成就。 1.5 货币与税收 了解中外历史上货币发行和使用情况，以及现代世界货币体系的 形成；了解中国古代赋税制度的演变；了解关税、个人所得税制度的 产生及其在中国的实行。 （2017年版2020年修订） 1.6 基层治理与社会保障 了解中国古代以赋役征发为首要目的的户籍制度，以及有代表性 的基层管理组织；知道中国古代王朝在社会救济和优抚方面采取的重 要措施；知道西方主要国家基层治理的特点及其由来；了解现代社会 保障制度的产生及其实行情况。 【教学提示】 1. 本模块的教学内容主要涉及历史上的国家制度，教师在教学 时，要注意引导学生探明某一制度产生的历史背景，以及与该制度有 关的历史渊源；在了解该制度基本内容的基础上，重点分析这一制度 的特点及作用，并认识该制度对当时及以后的影响。 2. 教师要以唯物史观为指导，从历史发展的角度引导学生认识 历史上的国家制度和社会治理的措施。一是要从历史的角度考虑具体 的国情和当时的社会状况，明了某一制度创立所要解决的社会问题； 二是要对某一制度的创新之处和存在的缺陷进行辩证的分析；三是要 注意某一制度是否在以后有不断完善或问题暴露、积累、激化的情况 等；四是对不同国家制度进行比较时，要避免简单的类比和抽象的优 劣评判，通过比较，使学生更清楚地认识不同国家各自的特点以及相 互之间的异同。如，通过了解商鞅、王安石、康有为等人的主张，对 商鞅变法、王安石变法、戊戌变法、明治维新等进行比较分析。

curriculum_points:
KC-5.3.II.i
Reconstruction and the Civil War ended slavery, altered relationships between the states and the federal government, and led to debates over new definitions of citizenship, particularly regarding the rights of African Americans, women, and other minorities.

KC-5.3.II.A
The 13th Amendment abolished slavery, while the 14th and 15th amendments granted African Americans citizenship, equal protection under the laws, and voting rights.

KC-5.3.II.C
Efforts by radical and moderate Republicans to change the balance of power between Congress and the presidency and to reorder race relations in the defeated South yielded some short-term successes. Reconstruction opened up political opportunities and other leadership roles to former slaves, but it ultimately failed, due both to determined Southern resistance and the North’s waning resolve.

KC-5.3.II.E
Segregation, violence, Supreme Court decisions, and local political tactics progressively stripped away African American rights, but the 14th and 15th amendments eventually became the basis for court decisions upholding civil rights in the 20th century.

curriculum_points:
Component 1 – Written Exam
Written paper, 1 hour 30 minutes, 45 marks
This component is an externally set assessment, marked by Cambridge International.
Component 1 contains three questions based on two source documents provided with the exam paper. The source documents may present different perspectives on an issue of global significance.
Candidates answer all the questions.
Question 1 (5 marks) is a structured question based on two source documents. Candidates are required to read both sources and answer short questions that require candidates to demonstrate AO1 skills.
Question 2 (15 marks) requires a longer response based on one of the source documents. Candidates are required to focus on the evidence in the document and demonstrate AO1 skills.
Question 3 (25 marks) requires a longer, essay response based on the two source documents. Candidates are required to focus on the arguments and perspectives given in the documents and provide a reasoned judgement, demonstrating AO1 and AO3 skills.

In carrying out a critical and comparative analysis of the source material, candidates are assessed on their ability to:
• identify evidence, analyse its strengths and weaknesses and evaluate the evidence (AO1)
• identify and compare key components of arguments (AO1)
• analyse and compare perspectives (AO1)
• evaluate arguments and make judgements about arguments and perspectives (AO1)
• communicate clearly and logically (AO3).

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-transport-modes.subject: inquiry

Students in PYP 4-5 will be able to analyze how the interaction of air, water, and solar energy causes different weather phenomena and extreme weather events.

Students will be able to choreograph and perform a short dance sequence that uses space, dynamics, and relationship to express an idea or emotion (3-5).

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-drama-role.name: 戏剧与角色扮演

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-earth-sun-moon.name: 日地月系统

curriculum_points: Students in PYP 3-5 will be able to use models to explain the cyclical patterns of day and night, and the apparent movement of the sun and moon across the sky, caused by the Earth's rotation.

Students in PYP 4-5 will be able to investigate and explain the relationship between force, mass, and movement, and identify examples of friction and gravity in everyday situations.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-great-explorers.name: 伟大的探险家

curriculum_points: Students will investigate how natural processes (erosion, deposition, tectonic activity) shape Earth's physical features, and represent their findings through models or diagrams.
By the end of Grade 5, students will be able to analyze the relationship between specific landforms and human activity, explaining how people adapt to and modify their physical environment.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-life-cycles.name: 生命周期
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-life-cycles.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-life-cycles.domain: 生命世界 / Living World / Living World
curriculum_points: Students in PYP 2-4 will be able to observe, record, and represent the stages of life cycles for different living things (e.g., plants, insects, amphibians), identifying patterns of growth, change, and reproduction.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-mental-wellbeing.name: 心理福祉
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-mental-wellbeing.subject: inquiry

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-work-jobs.name: 工作与职业

Students will be able to analyze the interdependence of jobs within an economic system and the skills and education required for different roles. (Age 7-9)

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-deforestation.name: 森林砍伐

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-human-body.name: 人体系统

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-peace-education.name: 和平教育

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-peace-education.domain: 公平与和平 / Equity & Peace / Equity & Peace
curriculum_points: The IB aims to develop inquiring, knowledgeable and caring young people who help to create a better and more peaceful world.

Students will be able to compose original poetic pieces using figurative language and deliberate structural choices to express personal ideas and emotions (3-5).

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-sculpture.name: 雕塑与立体造型

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-symbols-meaning.name: 符号与意义

curriculum_points: Students will be able to recognize that symbols, signs, and images communicate meaning and identify examples from their own environment (K-2).
