inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-cities.domain: 组织与结构 / Organizations & Systems / Organizations
curriculum_points: Students will be able to investigate the key systems of an urban area (e.g., transportation, housing, waste management) and explain how they are interconnected. (Age 7-9)
Students will be able to design a model or plan for a sustainable city, considering the balance between human needs and environmental impact. (Age 9-11)

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-climate-change.name: 气候变化
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-climate-change.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-climate-change.domain: 环境问题 / Environmental Issues / Environmental Issues
curriculum_points: An inquiry into the natural world and its laws; the interaction between the natural world and human societies; how humans use their understanding of scientific principles.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-conflict-resolution.name: 冲突解决
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-conflict-resolution.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-conflict-resolution.domain: 关系与社群 / Relationships & Community / Relationships
curriculum_points: Students in Lower Primary will be able to use 'I' statements to express their feelings during a disagreement and listen actively to the perspective of others.
Students in Upper Primary will be able to apply a range of conflict resolution strategies, such as negotiation and mediation, to resolve interpersonal problems peacefully and fairly.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-creative-writing.name: 创意写作
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-creative-writing.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-creative-writing.domain: 语言表达 / Language / Language Arts
curriculum_points: Students will be able to generate, draft, and illustrate simple written texts for enjoyment, using familiar structures and imaginative ideas (K-2).
Students will be able to apply the writing process (planning, drafting, revising, editing) to produce structured creative texts in various genres (3-5).

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-cultural-exchange.name: 文化交流
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-cultural-exchange.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-cultural-exchange.domain: 文明互鉴 / Civilizational Interaction / Civilizations
curriculum_points: Students will investigate how interaction between societies through trade, migration, or conquest leads to cultural diffusion and the exchange of ideas, arts, and innovations.
Learners will evaluate examples of cultural synthesis, demonstrating how elements from different cultures can combine to create new practices or forms of expression.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-decision-making.name: 决策过程
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-decision-making.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-decision-making.domain: 组织与结构 / Organizations & Systems / Organizations
curriculum_points: Students will be able to use a simple decision-making model (e.g., identify options, consider consequences) to make informed, ethical choices in familiar situations. (Age 7-9)
Students will be able to analyze how groups and organizations make decisions, exploring concepts of consensus, voting, and representation. (Age 9-11)

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-diaspora.name: 移民与散居
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-diaspora.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-diaspora.domain: 探索与迁徙 / Exploration & Migration / Exploration & Migration
curriculum_points: Students will explore the concepts of migration and diaspora, investigating the reasons why groups of people move and the effects on both the communities they leave and those they join.
Learners will demonstrate an understanding of how diaspora communities maintain and adapt cultural traditions, contributing to cultural diversity in their new locations.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-digital-art.name: 数字艺术
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-digital-art.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-digital-art.domain: 视觉艺术 / Visual Arts / Visual Arts
curriculum_points: Students will be able to use basic digital tools (e.g., drawing apps, cameras) to create, capture, and modify simple images (K-2).
Students will be able to create a digital art piece or composition, demonstrating an understanding of layering, editing, and digital effects to enhance expression (3-5).

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-ecosystem-balance.name: 生态平衡
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-ecosystem-balance.subject: inquiry
curriculum_points: An inquiry into the natural world and its laws; the interaction between the natural world (physical and biological) and human societies.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-electricity.name: 电与磁
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-electricity.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-electricity.domain: 物理世界 / Physical World / Physical World
curriculum_points: Students in PYP 3-4 will be able to build simple circuits using batteries, wires, and bulbs, and identify materials that are conductors or insulators of electricity.
Students in PYP 5 will be able to investigate how electricity is generated and transformed in their local environment, and propose ways to use it safely and responsibly.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-endangered.name: 濒危物种
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-endangered.subject: inquiry
curriculum_points: An inquiry into rights and responsibilities in the struggle to share finite resources with other people and with other living things; communities and the relationships within and between them.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-energy-forms.name: 能量形式
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-energy-forms.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-energy-forms.domain: 物理世界 / Physical World / Physical World
curriculum_points: Students in PYP 3-5 will be able to identify different forms of energy (e.g., heat, light, kinetic, chemical) and provide examples of energy transfer and transformation in simple systems.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-fair-trade.name: 公平贸易
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-fair-trade.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-fair-trade.domain: 公平与和平 / Equity & Peace / Equity & Peace
curriculum_points: An inquiry into the interconnectedness of human-made systems and communities; societal decision-making; economic activities and their impact on humankind.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-fairness.name: 公平与正义
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-fairness.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-fairness.domain: 权利与责任 / Rights & Responsibilities / Rights & Responsibilities
curriculum_points: Students will be able to identify examples of fairness and unfairness in familiar situations and explain their reasoning using the language of rights and responsibilities.
Students will be able to analyze real-world scenarios to understand issues of justice, and propose actions that promote equity and inclusive practices within their sphere of influence.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-global-citizenship.name: 全球公民
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-global-citizenship.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-global-citizenship.domain: 公平与和平 / Equity & Peace / Equity & Peace
curriculum_points: The IB aims to develop inquiring, knowledgeable and caring young people who help to create a better and more peaceful world through intercultural understanding and respect.
Students become active, compassionate and lifelong learners who understand that other people, with their differences, can also be right.

An inquiry into rights and responsibilities in the struggle to share finite resources; communities and the relationships within and between them; access to equal opportunities; peace and conflict resolution.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-global-networks.name: 全球网络
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-global-networks.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-global-networks.domain: 交通与通信 / Transport & Communication / Transport & Communication
curriculum_points: Students will be able to identify examples of global networks (e.g., trade, communication, transportation) and describe how they connect people and countries. (Age 7-9)
Students will be able to investigate a global issue (e.g., supply chains, news dissemination) to understand the complexity and interdependence of worldwide systems. (Age 9-11)

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-government.name: 政府与治理
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-government.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-government.domain: 社会组织 / Social Organization / Social Organization
curriculum_points: Students will be able to identify the basic functions and structures of government (e.g., local, national) and explain how they serve the needs of a community. (Age 9-11)
Students will be able to investigate and compare different forms of governance within their own and other societies, using key concepts such as function and responsibility.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-historical-change.name: 历史变迁
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-historical-change.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-historical-change.domain: 时间与历史 / Time & History / Time & History
curriculum_points: Students will analyze cause and effect by investigating the reasons for, and consequences of, a significant historical event or technological discovery.
Learners will compare past and present situations, identifying continuity and change over time in aspects such as social organization, technology, and beliefs.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-human-geography.name: 人文地理
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-human-geography.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-human-geography.domain: 地理与空间 / Place & Geography / Place & Geography
curriculum_points: Students will examine patterns of population distribution and density, formulating questions about the factors (e.g., resources, economic opportunity) that influence where people live.
Learners will compare different types of human settlements (rural, urban, suburban) and communicate how these communities are organized to meet human needs.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-internet-basics.name: 互联网初识
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-internet-basics.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-internet-basics.domain: 交通与通信 / Transport & Communication / Transport & Communication
curriculum_points: Students will be able to explain, in simple terms, how the internet functions as a network for finding and sharing information. (Age 7-9)
Students will be able to demonstrate digital citizenship by applying safe, ethical, and responsible practices when using online resources and communication tools. (Age 9-11)

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-invention-impact.name: 发明与社会影响
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-invention-impact.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-invention-impact.domain: 科学与技术 / Science & Technology / Science & Technology
curriculum_points: Students in PYP 4-5 will be able to research a significant invention or innovation, explaining the scientific principles behind it and evaluating its positive and negative consequences on society and the environment.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-myths-legends.name: 神话与传说
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-myths-legends.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-myths-legends.domain: 文化与信仰 / Culture & Beliefs / Culture & Beliefs
curriculum_points: Students will be able to listen to and retell myths or legends, identifying central characters and events (K-2).
Students will be able to compare myths and legends from different cultures, exploring how they explain natural phenomena, teach lessons, and express cultural identity (3-5).

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-solar-system.name: 太阳系
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-solar-system.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-solar-system.domain: 地球与宇宙 / Earth & Space / Earth & Space
curriculum_points: Students in PYP 4-5 will be able to describe the components of our solar system (sun, planets, moons) and compare celestial bodies based on their relative size, position, and composition.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-supply-demand.name: 供给与需求
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-supply-demand.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-supply-demand.domain: 经济活动 / Economic Systems / Economic Systems
curriculum_points: Students will be able to describe, using simple examples, how the price or availability of a good can be influenced by supply (how much there is) and demand (how many people want it). (Age 7-9)
Students will be able to conduct a basic investigation into a local market to observe the principles of supply and demand in action. (Age 9-11)

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-sustainability.name: 可持续发展
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-sustainability.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-sustainability.domain: 资源与可持续 / Resources & Sustainability / Resources
curriculum_points: An inquiry into rights and responsibilities in the struggle to share finite resources with other people and with other living things; economic activities and their impact on humankind and the environment.

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-theatre.name: 戏剧表演
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-theatre.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-theatre.domain: 表演艺术 / Performing Arts / Performing Arts
curriculum_points: Students will be able to participate in guided dramatic play and simple performances, understanding the role of an audience (K-2).
Students will be able to contribute to a collaborative theatre performance, taking on specific responsibilities (e.g., actor, designer, stagehand) and reflecting on the process (3-5).

inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-world-heritage.name: 世界遗产
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-world-heritage.subject: inquiry
inquiry-ib-pyp-pyp-world-heritage.domain: 文明互鉴 / Civilizational Interaction / Civilizations
curriculum_points: Students will research sites designated as UNESCO World Heritage, explaining their cultural or natural significance and the reasons for their preservation.
Learners will develop and present a case for a local site to be considered for heritage protection, identifying its value to community identity and global heritage.

math-cam-primary-2d-shapes.name: 二维图形
math-cam-primary-2d-shapes.subject: math
math-cam-primary-2d-shapes.domain: 几何与测量 / Geometry & Measure / Geometry & Measure

math-cam-primary-counting.name: 计数与数感
math-cam-primary-counting.subject: math
curriculum_points: Learners explore the five principles of counting and develop number fluency, demonstrating flexibility, efficiency and accuracy in the computational strategies that they choose.

Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity. For example, interpret P(1+r)^n as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.

HSA-SSE.A.2 Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it. For example, see x^4 – y^4 as (x^2)^2 – (y^2)^2, thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x^2 – y^2)(x^2 + y^2).

curriculum_points: HSA-SSE.A.2 Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it. For example, see x^4 – y^4 as (x^2)^2 – (y^2)^2, thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x^2 – y^2)(x^2 + y^2).

Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines. b. Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines. c. Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions. For example the expression 1.15^t can be rewritten as (1.15^(1/12))^(12t) ≈ 1.012^(12t) to reveal the approximate equivalent monthly interest rate if the annual rate is 15%.

Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.
HSF-IF.B.6 Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

G-GPE.B.4 Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically. math-h-trigonometry-solution.subject: math

三角函数是描述周期现象的重要数学模型，在数学和其他领域中都有广泛的应用。

math-ib-dp-dp-ai-3d-geom.name: 三维几何
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-3d-geom.subject: math
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-3d-geom.domain: 几何与三角 / Geometry & Trig / Geometry & Trig
curriculum_points: Solve problems involving points, lines, and planes in three dimensions using vector and Cartesian forms (AO2).
Calculate angles between lines and planes, and distances from a point to a line or plane in three-dimensional space.

math-ib-dp-dp-ai-correlation.name: 相关与回归
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-correlation.subject: math
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-correlation.domain: 统计与概率 / Stats & Probability / Stats & Prob
curriculum_points: Calculate and interpret the Pearson’s product-moment correlation coefficient (r) and the equation of the regression line y on x (AO2).
Make predictions using the regression line and understand the dangers of extrapolation and the distinction between correlation and causation.

math-ib-dp-dp-ai-deriv-basic.name: 基本导数
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-deriv-basic.subject: math
curriculum_points: Differentiate functions of the form f(x) = ax^n, sin x, cos x, e^x, and ln x, and apply rules for sums and constant multiples (AO1).
Use differentiation to find equations of tangents and normals, and to identify intervals where a function is increasing or decreasing.

math-ib-dp-dp-ai-descriptive.name: 描述统计
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-descriptive.subject: math
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-descriptive.domain: 统计与概率 / Stats & Probability / Stats & Prob
curriculum_points: Calculate, interpret, and compare descriptive statistics for univariate data, including measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and dispersion (range, interquartile range, variance, standard deviation) (AO2).
Construct and analyze box-and-whisker plots and cumulative frequency graphs to summarize and compare data sets.

math-ib-dp-dp-ai-exp-log.name: 指数与对数
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-exp-log.subject: math
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-exp-log.domain: 数与代数 / Number & Algebra / Number & Algebra
curriculum_points: Manipulate and solve exponential and logarithmic equations to model growth and decay phenomena, such as population growth and radioactive decay (AO2).
Sketch and interpret graphs of exponential and logarithmic functions, identifying key features such as asymptotes and intercepts.

math-ib-dp-dp-ai-finance.name: 金融数学（复利/年金）
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-finance.subject: math
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-finance.domain: 数与代数 / Number & Algebra / Number & Algebra
curriculum_points: Solve problems in financial mathematics involving compound interest, annuities, amortization, and depreciation using appropriate technology (AO3).
Interpret and calculate the real purchasing power of money, considering inflation, in financial decision-making.

math-ib-dp-dp-ai-linear-quad.name: 一次/二次函数
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-linear-quad.subject: math
curriculum_points: Solve systems of linear equations and quadratic equations, both analytically and graphically, and interpret the solutions in context (AO2).
Analyze and model relationships between variables using linear and quadratic functions, determining key features such as vertex and axis of symmetry.

math-ib-dp-dp-ai-models.name: 指数/三角模型
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-models.subject: math
curriculum_points: Construct and interpret exponential and trigonometric models (sine and cosine) to represent periodic or growth/decay behavior in real-world data (AO3).
Use trigonometric models to solve problems involving periodic phenomena such as tides, seasonal temperatures, or harmonic motion.

math-ib-dp-dp-ai-number.name: 指数/科学计数法/近似
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-number.subject: math
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-number.domain: 数与代数 / Number & Algebra / Number & Algebra
curriculum_points: Use and interpret scientific notation, decimal approximations, and significant figures to represent and communicate quantitative information accurately (AO2).
Apply rounding conventions and percentage error calculations to assess the reasonableness of solutions in applied contexts.

math-ib-dp-dp-ai-rate-change.name: 变化率
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-rate-change.subject: math
curriculum_points: Interpret the derivative as an instantaneous rate of change in applied contexts, such as velocity, acceleration, and marginal cost (AO2).
Estimate rates of change from tables and graphs, and use difference quotients to approximate derivatives.

math-ib-dp-dp-ai-sequences.name: 等差与等比数列
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-sequences.subject: math
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-sequences.domain: 数与代数 / Number & Algebra / Number & Algebra
curriculum_points: Model real-world situations using arithmetic and geometric sequences and series, including applications in finance and growth (AO3).
Solve problems involving the nth term and the sum of n terms for arithmetic and geometric sequences.

math-ib-dp-dp-ai-trig-app.name: 三角应用
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-trig-app.subject: math
math-ib-dp-dp-ai-trig-app.domain: 几何与三角 / Geometry & Trig / Geometry & Trig
curriculum_points: Apply trigonometric ratios and the sine and cosine rules to solve practical problems involving non-right-angled triangles, including navigation and surveying (AO3).
Use trigonometric functions to model and solve problems involving areas of triangles and lengths of arcs and sectors.

curriculum_points: HSF-BF.A.1.c Compose functions. For example, if T(y) is the temperature in the atmosphere as a function of height, and h(t) is the height of a weather balloon as a function of time, then T(h(t)) is the temperature at the location of the weather balloon as a function of time.

HSF-BF.B.4 Find inverse functions. a. Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple function f that has an inverse and write an expression for the inverse. For example, f(x) =2x^3 or f(x) = (x+1)/(x-1) for x ≠ 1.

math-ap-bc-power-series.subject: math
curriculum_points:
TOPIC 1.1
Introducing Calculus: Can Change Occur at an Instant?
Required Course Content
ENDURING UNDERSTANDING
CHA-1
Calculus allows us to generalize knowledge about motion to diverse problems involving change.
LEARNING OBJECTIVE ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE
CHA-1.A CHA-1.A.1
Interpret the rate of change at an instant in terms of average rates of change over intervals containing that instant. Calculus uses limits to understand and model dynamic change.
CHA-1.A.2
Because an average rate of change divides the change in one variable by the change in another, the average rate of change is undefined at a point where the change in the independent variable would be zero.
CHA-1.A.3
The limit concept allows us to define instantaneous rate of change in terms of average rates of change.

TOPIC 2.1
Defining Average and Instantaneous Rates of Change at a Point
Required Course Content
ENDURING UNDERSTANDING
CHA-2
Derivatives allow us to determine rates of change at an instant by applying limits to knowledge about rates of change over intervals.
LEARNING OBJECTIVE ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE
CHA-2.A CHA-2.A.1
Determine average rates of change using difference quotients. The difference quotients f(a+h)−f(a) / h and f(x)−f(a) / x−a express the average rate of change of a function over an interval.
CHA-2.B CHA-2.B.1
Represent the derivative of a function as the limit of a difference quotient. The instantaneous rate of change of a function at x=a can be expressed by lim h→0 f(a+h)−f(a) / h or lim x→a f(x)−f(a) / x−a, provided the limit exists. These are equivalent forms of the definition of the derivative and are denoted f′(a).

math-ap-cab-antiderivative.subject: math
math-ap-cab-antiderivative.domain: Unit 6-7 积分与微分方程 Integration & DE
curriculum_points:
TOPIC 3.1 The Chain Rule
SUGGESTED SKILL
Implementing Mathematical Processes 1.C
Identify an appropriate mathematical rule or procedure based on the classification of a given expression (e.g., Use the chain rule to find the derivative of a composite function).

FUN-3.C Calculate derivatives of compositions of differentiable functions.
FUN-3.C.1 The chain rule provides a way to differentiate composite functions.

UNIT 3 Developing Understanding
In this unit, students learn how to differentiate composite functions using the chain rule and apply that understanding to determine derivatives of implicit and inverse functions. Students need to understand that for composite functions, y is a function of u while u is a function of x. Leibniz notation for the chain rule, dy/dx = dy/du * du/dx, accounts for these relationships.

UNIT 3 Preparing for the AP Exam
Mastery of the chain rule and its applications is essential for success on the AP Exam. The chain rule will be the target of assessment for many questions and a necessary step along the way for others. One common error is not recognizing when the chain rule applies, especially in composite functions such as sin²x, tan(2x - 1), and e^(x²).

curriculum_points:
SL 1.6
Content Guidance, clarification and syllabus links
Simple deductive proof, numerical and algebraic; how to lay out a left-hand side to right-hand side (LHS to RHS) proof.
The symbols and notation for equality and identity.
LHS to RHS proofs require students to begin with the left-hand side expression and transform this using known algebraic steps into the expression on the right-hand side (or vice versa).
Example: Show that (x−3)2+5≡x2−6x+14.
Students will be expected to show how they can check a result including a check of their own results.

AHL 1.15
Content Guidance, clarification and syllabus links
Proof by mathematical induction.
Proof should be incorporated throughout the course where appropriate.
Mathematical induction links specifically to a wide variety of topics, for example complex numbers, differentiation, sums of sequences and divisibility.
Proof by contradiction.
Examples: Irrationality of 3; irrationality of the cube root of 5; Euclid’s proof of an infinite number of prime numbers; if a is a rational number and b is an irrational number, then a+b is an irrational number.
Use of a counterexample to show that a statement is not always true.
Example: Consider the set P of numbers of the form n2+41n+41, n∈ℕ, show that not all elements of P are prime.
Example: Show that the following statement is not always true: there are no positive integer solutions to the equation x2+y2=10.
It is not sufficient to state the counterexample alone. Students must explain why their example is a counterexample.

science-cam-primary-forces-p.name: 力与运动

Pf.02 Notice that some forces need contact between two objects, but magnetic forces can act at a distance.
Pf.03 Observe how magnets attract or repel each other and attract some materials and not others.
Pf.04 Compare and group together a variety of everyday materials on the basis of whether they are attracted to a magnet, and identify some magnetic materials.

Pf.06 Predict whether two magnets will attract or repel each other, depending on which poles are facing.
Pf.07 Explain that unsupported objects fall towards the Earth because of the force of gravity acting between the Earth and the falling object.
Pf.08 Identify the effects of air resistance, water resistance and friction, that act between moving surfaces.
Pf.09 Recognise that some mechanisms, including levers, pulleys and gears, allow a smaller force to have a greater effect.

science-cam-primary-human-body-p.name: 人体

Bh.04 Identify that humans and some other animals have skeletons and muscles for support, protection and movement.
Bh.05 Describe the ways in which nutrients and water are transported within animals, including humans.
Bh.06 Describe the changes as humans develop to old age.

5-LS2-1: Develop a model to describe the movement of matter among plants, animals, decomposers, and the environment.

science-us-k5-motion-forces-k5.name: 力与运动

MS-ESS2-6. Develop and use a model to describe how unequal heating and rotation of the Earth cause patterns of atmospheric and oceanic circulation that determine regional climates.

science-ib-myp-myp-atoms-molecules.name: 原子与分子
science-ib-myp-myp-atoms-molecules.subject: science
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 2-4 will be able to describe the basic structure of an atom (protons, neutrons, electrons) and use the periodic table to identify elements by their atomic number and mass.
Students will be able to differentiate between atoms, elements, molecules, and compounds, and represent simple molecules using chemical formulas (e.g., H2O, CO2).

science-ib-myp-myp-energy.name: 能量
science-ib-myp-myp-energy.subject: science
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 1-4 will be able to identify different forms of energy (e.g., kinetic, potential, thermal, chemical) and describe energy transfers and transformations in simple systems.
Students will be able to apply the principle of conservation of energy to explain that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only changed from one form to another.

science-ib-myp-myp-experiment-design.name: 实验设计
science-ib-myp-myp-experiment-design.subject: science
science-ib-myp-myp-experiment-design.domain: 科学探究 / Scientific Inquiry / Scientific Inquiry
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 2-5 will be able to design a controlled experiment, identifying and justifying the control of variables (independent, dependent, controlled) to ensure a fair test.
Students will be able to select appropriate equipment and methods, and describe a logical, safe procedure to collect sufficient and relevant data.

science-ib-myp-myp-human-body.name: 人体系统
science-ib-myp-myp-human-body.subject: science
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 2-4 will be able to describe the structure and function of at least two major human body systems (e.g., digestive, respiratory, circulatory) and explain how they interact to maintain health.
Students will be able to investigate a lifestyle factor (e.g., diet, exercise) and analyze its impact on the efficient functioning of a chosen body system.

science-us-ms-electromagnetic.name: 电磁
science-us-ms-electromagnetic.subject: science
science-us-ms-electromagnetic.domain: 物质科学 / Physical Sciences / Physical Sciences
curriculum_points: MS-PS4-3. Integrate qualitative scientific and technical information to support the claim that digitized signals are a more reliable way to encode and transmit information than analog signals.

science-us-ms-evolution-ms.name: 进化
science-us-ms-evolution-ms.subject: science
science-us-ms-evolution-ms.domain: 生命科学 / Life Sciences / Life Sciences
curriculum_points: MS-LS4-1. Analyze and interpret data for patterns in the fossil record that document the existence, diversity, extinction, and change of life forms throughout the history of life on Earth under the assumption that natural laws operate today as in the past.

MS-LS4-2. Apply scientific ideas to construct an explanation for the anatomical similarities and differences among modern organisms and between modern and fossil organisms to infer evolutionary relationships.

MS-LS4-3. Analyze displays of pictorial data to compare patterns of similarities in the embryological development across multiple species to identify relationships not evident in the fully formed anatomy.

MS-LS4-4. Construct an explanation based on evidence that describes how genetic variations of traits in a population increase some individuals’ probability of surviving and reproducing in a specific environment.
MS-LS4-5. Gather and synthesize information about the technologies that have changed the way humans influence the inheritance of desired traits in organisms.
MS-LS4-6. Use mathematical representations to support explanations of how natural selection may lead to increases and decreases of specific traits in populations over time.

science-us-ms-heredity-ms.name: 遗传
science-us-ms-heredity-ms.subject: science
science-us-ms-heredity-ms.domain: 生命科学 / Life Sciences / Life Sciences
curriculum_points: MS-LS3-1. Develop and use a model to describe why structural changes to genes (mutations) located on chromosomes may affect proteins and may result in harmful, beneficial, or neutral effects to the structure and function of the organism.
MS-LS3-2. Develop and use a model to describe why asexual reproduction results in offspring with identical genetic information and sexual reproduction results in offspring with genetic variation.

science-us-ms-human-impact-ms.name: 人类影响
science-us-ms-human-impact-ms.subject: science
science-us-ms-human-impact-ms.domain: 地球与空间 / Earth & Space / Earth & Space
curriculum_points: MS-ESS3-1. Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for how the uneven distributions of Earth’s mineral, energy, and groundwater resources are the result of past and current geoscience processes.
MS-ESS3-2. Analyze and interpret data on natural hazards to forecast future catastrophic events and inform the development of technologies to mitigate their effects.
MS-ESS3-3. Apply scientific principles to design a method for monitoring and minimizing a human impact on the environment.
MS-ESS3-4. Construct an argument supported by evidence for how increases in human population and per-capita consumption of natural resources impact Earth’s systems.

science-us-ms-optimization.name: 优化设计
science-us-ms-optimization.subject: science
curriculum_points: MS-ETS1-3. Analyze data from tests to determine similarities and differences among several design solutions to identify the best characteristics of each that can be combined into a new solution to better meet the criteria for success.
MS-ETS1-4. Develop a model to generate data for iterative testing and modification of a proposed object, tool, or process such that an optimal design can be achieved.

science-us-ms-waves-ms.name: 波动
science-us-ms-waves-ms.subject: science
science-us-ms-waves-ms.domain: 物质科学 / Physical Sciences / Physical Sciences
curriculum_points: MS-PS4-1. Use mathematical representations to describe a simple model for waves that includes how the amplitude of a wave is related to the energy in a wave.
MS-PS4-2. Develop and use a model to describe that waves are reflected, absorbed, or transmitted through various materials.

science-cam-lsec-solar-system-l.name: 太阳系
science-cam-lsec-solar-system-l.subject: science

curriculum_points: Strand: Physics - The Earth and beyond.

science-ib-myp-myp-chemical-reactions.name: 化学反应
science-ib-myp-myp-chemical-reactions.subject: science
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to identify evidence of a chemical reaction (e.g., color change, gas production, temperature change) and distinguish it from a physical change.
Students will be able to write simple word equations and balanced chemical equations for common reactions, such as combustion or acid-metal reactions.

science-ib-myp-myp-data-analysis.name: 数据分析
science-ib-myp-myp-data-analysis.subject: science
science-ib-myp-myp-data-analysis.domain: 科学探究 / Scientific Inquiry / Scientific Inquiry
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 1-5 will be able to process qualitative and/or quantitative data by constructing appropriate graphs (e.g., bar, line) and calculating means.
Students will be able to identify trends and patterns in data, draw conclusions supported by evidence, and evaluate the reliability of their method.

science-ib-myp-myp-ecology.name: 生态学
science-ib-myp-myp-ecology.subject: science
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 1-4 will be able to construct and analyze food chains and webs to illustrate the flow of energy and interdependence of organisms within an ecosystem.
Students will be able to investigate an environmental factor (e.g., pH, temperature) and assess its impact on a specific population within a local ecosystem.

science-ib-myp-myp-environmental-sci.name: 环境科学
science-ib-myp-myp-environmental-sci.subject: science
science-ib-myp-myp-environmental-sci.domain: 科技与社会 / Science & Society / Science & Society
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 2-5 will be able to analyze human impacts (e.g., pollution, deforestation, climate change) on a specific ecosystem and propose scientifically sound mitigation strategies.
Students will be able to evaluate the sustainability of a resource management practice by considering its environmental, economic, and social impacts.

science-ib-myp-myp-waves.name: 波动
science-ib-myp-myp-waves.subject: science
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to describe wave properties (wavelength, frequency, amplitude) and differentiate between transverse and longitudinal waves using examples like light and sound.
Students will be able to explain how the properties of waves (e.g., reflection, refraction) are applied in technologies such as mirrors, lenses, or ultrasound imaging.

science-ib-myp-myp-acids-bases.name: 酸碱
science-ib-myp-myp-acids-bases.subject: science
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 3-4 will be able to use the pH scale to classify solutions as acidic, basic, or neutral, and safely use indicators to test common household substances.
Students will be able to describe the properties of acids and bases, and explain the process of neutralization with examples from everyday life (e.g., indigestion remedies).

science-ib-myp-myp-electricity.name: 电路与电磁
science-ib-myp-myp-electricity.subject: science
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to construct simple series and parallel circuits using schematic diagrams and explain the effect of adding components on current and brightness.
Students will be able to describe the relationship between magnetism and electricity, and explain the principle of electromagnetic induction in generators.

science-ib-myp-myp-ethics-science.name: 科学伦理
science-ib-myp-myp-ethics-science.subject: science
science-ib-myp-myp-ethics-science.domain: 科技与社会 / Science & Society / Science & Society
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to discuss the ethical implications of a scientific development (e.g., genetic engineering, animal testing) by considering different stakeholder perspectives.
Students will be able to explain the importance of honesty, integrity, and peer review in the scientific process, and identify examples of ethical and unethical scientific conduct.

science-ib-myp-myp-evolution-intro.name: 进化入门
science-ib-myp-myp-evolution-intro.subject: science
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 3-5 will be able to explain the concept of natural selection as a mechanism for evolution, using specific examples of variation, adaptation, and environmental pressure.
Students will be able to evaluate different types of evidence (e.g., fossil records, anatomical similarities) that support the theory of evolution.

science-ib-myp-myp-genetics-intro.name: 遗传入门
science-ib-myp-myp-genetics-intro.subject: science
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 3-4 will be able to define and use basic genetic terminology, including gene, allele, dominant, recessive, genotype, and phenotype.
Students will be able to construct and interpret simple Punnett squares to predict the probability of inherited traits in offspring.

science-ib-myp-myp-scientific-writing.name: 科学写作
science-ib-myp-myp-scientific-writing.subject: science
science-ib-myp-myp-scientific-writing.domain: 科学探究 / Scientific Inquiry / Scientific Inquiry
curriculum_points: Students in MYP 1-5 will be able to structure a laboratory report with clear sections (aim, hypothesis, method, results, conclusion, evaluation).
Students will be able to communicate findings using scientific language and conventions, including proper units, terminology, and citations where appropriate.

tok-ib-dp-dp-aok-arts.name: 艺术
tok-ib-dp-dp-aok-arts.subject: tok
tok-ib-dp-dp-aok-arts.domain: 知识领域 / Areas of Knowledge / Areas of Knowledge
curriculum_points: Students will be able to analyse the role of imagination, emotion, and perception in the creation and interpretation of artistic knowledge.
Students will be able to evaluate different criteria used to judge artistic value and knowledge, considering the tension between subjective interpretation and objective standards.

tok-ib-dp-dp-aok-history.name: 历史
tok-ib-dp-dp-aok-history.subject: tok
tok-ib-dp-dp-aok-history.domain: 知识领域 / Areas of Knowledge / Areas of Knowledge
curriculum_points: Students will be able to analyse how historians construct knowledge through the selection, interpretation, and synthesis of evidence from the past.
Students will be able to evaluate the challenges of historical objectivity, including the role of perspective, bias, and the influence of present values on historical narratives.

tok-ib-dp-dp-aok-human-sci.name: 人文科学
tok-ib-dp-dp-aok-human-sci.subject: tok
tok-ib-dp-dp-aok-human-sci.domain: 知识领域 / Areas of Knowledge / Areas of Knowledge
curriculum_points: Students will be able to assess the methodological challenges in the human sciences, such as the role of interpretation, the observer effect, and the difficulty of establishing causal laws.
Students will be able to compare the nature of evidence and explanation in the human sciences with that in the natural sciences.

tok-ib-dp-dp-aok-math.name: 数学
tok-ib-dp-dp-aok-math.subject: tok
tok-ib-dp-dp-aok-math.domain: 知识领域 / Areas of Knowledge / Areas of Knowledge
curriculum_points: Students will be able to explain the roles of axiomatic systems, deductive reasoning, and proof in establishing mathematical certainty and truth.
Students will be able to discuss the relationship between abstract mathematical concepts and their application in the real world, considering whether mathematics is discovered or invented.

tok-ib-dp-dp-aok-natural-sci.name: 自然科学
tok-ib-dp-dp-aok-natural-sci.subject: tok
tok-ib-dp-dp-aok-natural-sci.domain: 知识领域 / Areas of Knowledge / Areas of Knowledge
curriculum_points: Students will be able to evaluate the roles of observation, experimentation, and falsification in the construction of scientific knowledge, considering the provisional nature of scientific claims.
Students will be able to analyse how paradigms, models, and technological advances shape the methods and scope of the natural sciences.

tok-ib-dp-dp-knower-perspective.name: 知者视角
tok-ib-dp-dp-knower-perspective.subject: tok
tok-ib-dp-dp-knower-perspective.domain: 核心主题 / Core Theme / Core Theme
curriculum_points: Students will be able to analyse the role of personal and shared knowledge, and evaluate how factors such as emotion, reason, and culture shape the knower's perspective.
Students will be able to reflect on their own perspectives as knowers and identify how their position in the world influences their understanding and claims.

tok-ib-dp-dp-knowledge-claims.name: 知识声明
tok-ib-dp-dp-knowledge-claims.subject: tok
tok-ib-dp-dp-knowledge-claims.domain: 核心主题 / Core Theme / Core Theme
curriculum_points: Students will be able to distinguish between shared and personal knowledge claims, and construct meaningful knowledge questions that arise from them.
Students will be able to evaluate the implications of asserting 'I know' versus 'I believe' in different contexts.

tok-ib-dp-dp-tok-exhibition.name: TOK 展览（IA）
tok-ib-dp-dp-tok-exhibition.subject: tok
curriculum_points: Students will be able to select a prescribed title and curate an exhibition of three objects that effectively explore knowledge questions arising from it in a concrete, real-world context.
Students will be able to produce a written commentary that clearly justifies the selection of each object and explains its specific connection to the chosen title and relevant TOK concepts.

tok-ib-dp-dp-opt-indigenous.name: 本土社会
tok-ib-dp-dp-opt-indigenous.subject: tok
tok-ib-dp-dp-opt-indigenous.domain: 可选主题 / Optional Themes / Optional Themes
curriculum_points: Students will be able to analyse distinctive features of indigenous knowledge systems, such as holistic perspectives, oral tradition, and connections to land and community.
Students will be able to reflect on the implications of different knowledge systems for understanding issues of sustainability, identity, and cultural preservation.

tok-ib-dp-dp-opt-language.name: 语言与知识
tok-ib-dp-dp-opt-language.subject: tok
tok-ib-dp-dp-opt-language.domain: 可选主题 / Optional Themes / Optional Themes
curriculum_points: Students will be able to analyse how language shapes thought, classification, and the communication of knowledge within and between communities.
Students will be able to evaluate the challenges of translation, ambiguity, and the use of metaphor in the pursuit of precise knowledge.

tok-ib-dp-dp-opt-politics.name: 政治与知识
tok-ib-dp-dp-opt-politics.subject: tok
tok-ib-dp-dp-opt-politics.domain: 可选主题 / Optional Themes / Optional Themes
curriculum_points: Students will be able to analyse how power structures and ideologies influence the production, validation, and control of knowledge within societies.
Students will be able to evaluate the concept of 'official knowledge' and the role of education, media, and institutions in shaping public understanding.

tok-ib-dp-dp-opt-religion.name: 宗教与知识
tok-ib-dp-dp-opt-religion.subject: tok
tok-ib-dp-dp-opt-religion.domain: 可选主题 / Optional Themes / Optional Themes
curriculum_points: Students will be able to compare the nature of faith-based knowledge claims with those based on evidence and reason, analysing their different foundations and methods of justification.
Students will be able to discuss the role of religious knowledge systems in providing frameworks for understanding the world and human experience.

tok-ib-dp-dp-opt-technology.name: 技术与知识
tok-ib-dp-dp-opt-technology.subject: tok
tok-ib-dp-dp-opt-technology.domain: 可选主题 / Optional Themes / Optional Themes
curriculum_points: Students will be able to analyse the impact of technological tools and media on the production, acquisition, and dissemination of knowledge across various AOKs.
Students will be able to evaluate ethical considerations and the potential for bias inherent in the algorithms and design of knowledge technologies.

tok-ib-dp-dp-tok-essay.name: TOK Essay（1600 词）
tok-ib-dp-dp-tok-essay.subject: tok
curriculum_points: Students will be able to construct a focused, coherent, and critical argument in response to a prescribed essay title, integrating analysis of specific Areas of Knowledge and relevant TOK concepts.
Students will be able to demonstrate independent thinking, precise use of TOK terminology, and effective evaluation of competing perspectives and implications in their essay.

tok-ib-dp-dp-truth-belief.name: 真理与信念
tok-ib-dp-dp-truth-belief.subject: tok
tok-ib-dp-dp-truth-belief.domain: 核心主题 / Core Theme / Core Theme
curriculum_points: Students will be able to compare and contrast theories of truth (e.g., correspondence, coherence, pragmatic) and analyse their applicability in different Areas of Knowledge.
Students will be able to critically examine the relationship between justification, evidence, belief, and truth.
